<h1 id="google-sheets-api">Google Sheets API v4</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Reads and writes Google Sheets.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://sheets.googleapis.com/">https://sheets.googleapis.com/</a>

<a href="https://developers.google.com/terms/">Terms of service</a>
Web: <a href="https://google.com">Google</a> 
License: <a href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/">Creative Commons Attribution 3.0</a>

<a href="https://developers.google.com/sheets/">External documentation</a>

# Authentication

- oAuth2 authentication. Oauth 2.0 implicit authentication

    - Flow: implicit
    - Authorization URL = [https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth](https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive|See, edit, create, and delete all of your Google Drive files|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file|See, edit, create, and delete only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly|See and download all your Google Drive files|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets|See, edit, create, and delete all your Google Sheets spreadsheets|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly|See all your Google Sheets spreadsheets|

- oAuth2 authentication. Oauth 2.0 authorizationCode authentication

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth](https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth)
    - Token URL = [https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/token](https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive|See, edit, create, and delete all of your Google Drive files|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file|See, edit, create, and delete only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly|See and download all your Google Drive files|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets|See, edit, create, and delete all your Google Sheets spreadsheets|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly|See all your Google Sheets spreadsheets|

<h1 id="google-sheets-api-spreadsheets">spreadsheets</h1>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|key|query|string|false|API key. Your API key identifies your project and provides you with API access, quota, and reports. Required unless you provide an OAuth 2.0 token.|
|oauth_token|query|string|false|OAuth 2.0 token for the current user.|
|prettyPrint|query|boolean|false|Returns response with indentations and line breaks.|
|quotaUser|query|string|false|Available to use for quota purposes for server-side applications. Can be any arbitrary string assigned to a user, but should not exceed 40 characters.|
|upload_protocol|query|string|false|Upload protocol for media (e.g. "raw", "multipart").|
|uploadType|query|string|false|Legacy upload protocol for media (e.g. "media", "multipart").|
|body|body|[Spreadsheet](#schemaspreadsheet)|false|none|
|» dataSources|body|[[DataSource](#schemadatasource)]|false|A list of external data sources connected with the spreadsheet.|
|» developerMetadata|body|[[DeveloperMetadata](#schemadevelopermetadata)]|false|The developer metadata associated with a spreadsheet.|
|» namedRanges|body|[[NamedRange](#schemanamedrange)]|false|The named ranges defined in a spreadsheet.|
|» properties|body|[SpreadsheetProperties](#schemaspreadsheetproperties)|false|Overall properties of a spreadsheet.|
|» sheets|body|[[Sheet](#schemasheet)]|false|The sheets that are part of a spreadsheet.|
|» spreadsheetId|body|string|false|The ID of the spreadsheet. This field is read-only.|
|» spreadsheetUrl|body|string|false|The url of the spreadsheet. This field is read-only.|

</aside>

## sheets.spreadsheets.get

<a id="opIdsheets.spreadsheets.get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}`

Returns the spreadsheet at the given ID. The caller must specify the spreadsheet ID. By default, data within grids is not returned. You can include grid data in one of 2 ways: * Specify a [field mask](https://developers.google.com/sheets/api/guides/field-masks) listing your desired fields using the `fields` URL parameter in HTTP * Set the includeGridData URL parameter to true. If a field mask is set, the `includeGridData` parameter is ignored For large spreadsheets, as a best practice, retrieve only the specific spreadsheet fields that you want. To retrieve only subsets of spreadsheet data, use the ranges URL parameter. Ranges are specified using [A1 notation](/sheets/api/guides/concepts#cell). You can define a single cell (for example, `A1`) or multiple cells (for example, `A1:D5`). You can also get cells from other sheets within the same spreadsheet (for example, `Sheet2!A1:C4`) or retrieve multiple ranges at once (for example, `?ranges=A1:D5&ranges=Sheet2!A1:C4`). Limiting the range returns only the portions of the spreadsheet that intersect the requested ranges.

<h3 id="sheetsspreadsheetsget-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spreadsheetId|path|string|true|The spreadsheet to request.|
|includeGridData|query|boolean|false|True if grid data should be returned. This parameter is ignored if a field mask was set in the request.|
|ranges|query|[string]|false|The ranges to retrieve from the spreadsheet.|
|$.xgafv|query|string|false|V1 error format.|
|access_token|query|string|false|OAuth access token.|
|alt|query|string|false|Data format for response.|
|callback|query|string|false|JSONP|
|fields|query|string|false|Selector specifying which fields to include in a partial response.|
|key|query|string|false|API key. Your API key identifies your project and provides you with API access, quota, and reports. Required unless you provide an OAuth 2.0 token.|
|oauth_token|query|string|false|OAuth 2.0 token for the current user.|
|prettyPrint|query|boolean|false|Returns response with indentations and line breaks.|
|quotaUser|query|string|false|Available to use for quota purposes for server-side applications. Can be any arbitrary string assigned to a user, but should not exceed 40 characters.|
|upload_protocol|query|string|false|Upload protocol for media (e.g. "raw", "multipart").|
|uploadType|query|string|false|Legacy upload protocol for media (e.g. "media", "multipart").|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|$.xgafv|1|
|$.xgafv|2|
|alt|json|
|alt|media|
|alt|proto|

`POST /v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}/developerMetadata:search`

Returns all developer metadata matching the specified DataFilter. If the provided DataFilter represents a DeveloperMetadataLookup object, this will return all DeveloperMetadata entries selected by it. If the DataFilter represents a location in a spreadsheet, this will return all developer metadata associated with locations intersecting that region.

> Body parameter

## sheets.spreadsheets.values.append

<a id="opIdsheets.spreadsheets.values.append"></a>

```bash

  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "majorDimension": "DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED",
    "range": "string",
    "values": [
      [
        null
      ]
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}/values/{range}:append`

Appends values to a spreadsheet. The input range is used to search for existing data and find a "table" within that range. Values will be appended to the next row of the table, starting with the first column of the table. See the [guide](/sheets/api/guides/values#appending_values) and [sample code](/sheets/api/samples/writing#append_values) for specific details of how tables are detected and data is appended. The caller must specify the spreadsheet ID, range, and a valueInputOption. The `valueInputOption` only controls how the input data will be added to the sheet (column-wise or row-wise), it does not influence what cell the data starts being written to.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "majorDimension": "DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED",
  "range": "string",
  "values": [
    [
      null
    ]
  ]
}
```

|» responseDateTimeRenderOption|body|string|false|Determines how dates, times, and durations in the response should be rendered. This is ignored if response_value_render_option is FORMATTED_VALUE. The default dateTime render option is SERIAL_NUMBER.|
|» responseValueRenderOption|body|string|false|Determines how values in the response should be rendered. The default render option is FORMATTED_VALUE.|
|» valueInputOption|body|string|false|How the input data should be interpreted.|


`POST /v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}:batchUpdate`

Applies one or more updates to the spreadsheet. Each request is validated before being applied. If any request is not valid then the entire request will fail and nothing will be applied. Some requests have replies to give you some information about how they are applied. The replies will mirror the requests. For example, if you applied 4 updates and the 3rd one had a reply, then the response will have 2 empty replies, the actual reply, and another empty reply, in that order. Due to the collaborative nature of spreadsheets, it is not guaranteed that the spreadsheet will reflect exactly your changes after this completes, however it is guaranteed that the updates in the request will be applied together atomically. Your changes may be altered with respect to collaborator changes. If there are no collaborators, the spreadsheet should reflect your changes.

<h3 id="sheetsspreadsheetsbatchupdate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spreadsheetId|path|string|true|The spreadsheet to apply the updates to.|
|$.xgafv|query|string|false|V1 error format.|
|access_token|query|string|false|OAuth access token.|
|alt|query|string|false|Data format for response.|
|callback|query|string|false|JSONP|
|fields|query|string|false|Selector specifying which fields to include in a partial response.|
|key|query|string|false|API key. Your API key identifies your project and provides you with API access, quota, and reports. Required unless you provide an OAuth 2.0 token.|
|oauth_token|query|string|false|OAuth 2.0 token for the current user.|
|prettyPrint|query|boolean|false|Returns response with indentations and line breaks.|
|quotaUser|query|string|false|Available to use for quota purposes for server-side applications. Can be any arbitrary string assigned to a user, but should not exceed 40 characters.|
|upload_protocol|query|string|false|Upload protocol for media (e.g. "raw", "multipart").|
|uploadType|query|string|false|Legacy upload protocol for media (e.g. "media", "multipart").|
|body|body|[BatchUpdateSpreadsheetRequest](#schemabatchupdatespreadsheetrequest)|false|none|
|» includeSpreadsheetInResponse|body|boolean|false|Determines if the update response should include the spreadsheet resource.|
|» requests|body|[[Request](#schemarequest)]|false|A list of updates to apply to the spreadsheet. Requests will be applied in the order they are specified. If any request is not valid, no requests will be applied.|
|» responseIncludeGridData|body|boolean|false|True if grid data should be returned. Meaningful only if include_spreadsheet_in_response is 'true'. This parameter is ignored if a field mask was set in the request.|
|» responseRanges|body|[string]|false|Limits the ranges included in the response spreadsheet. Meaningful only if include_spreadsheet_in_response is 'true'.|

`POST /v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}:getByDataFilter`

Returns the spreadsheet at the given ID. The caller must specify the spreadsheet ID. This method differs from GetSpreadsheet in that it allows selecting which subsets of spreadsheet data to return by specifying a dataFilters parameter. Multiple DataFilters can be specified. Specifying one or more data filters returns the portions of the spreadsheet that intersect ranges matched by any of the filters. By default, data within grids is not returned. You can include grid data one of 2 ways: * Specify a [field mask](https://developers.google.com/sheets/api/guides/field-masks) listing your desired fields using the `fields` URL parameter in HTTP * Set the includeGridData parameter to true. If a field mask is set, the `includeGridData` parameter is ignored For large spreadsheets, as a best practice, retrieve only the specific spreadsheet fields that you want.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dataFilters": [
    {
      "a1Range": "string",
      "developerMetadataLookup": {
        "locationMatchingStrategy": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_LOCATION_MATCHING_STRATEGY_UNSPECIFIED",
        "locationType": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_LOCATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
        "metadataId": 0,
        "metadataKey": "string",
        "metadataLocation": {
          "dimensionRange": {
            "dimension": "DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED",
            "endIndex": 0,
            "sheetId": 0,
            "startIndex": 0
          },
          "locationType": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_LOCATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
          "sheetId": 0,
          "spreadsheet": true
        },
        "metadataValue": "string",
        "visibility": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_VISIBILITY_UNSPECIFIED"
      },
      "gridRange": {
        "endColumnIndex": 0,
        "endRowIndex": 0,
        "sheetId": 0,
        "startColumnIndex": 0,
        "startRowIndex": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "includeGridData": true
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|chart|[EmbeddedChart](#schemaembeddedchart)|false|none|The chart that should be added to the spreadsheet, including the position where it should be placed. The chartId field is optional; if one is not set, an id will be randomly generated. (It is an error to specify the ID of an embedded object that already exists.)|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
    "sheetId": 0,
```


Creates a group over the specified range. If the requested range is a superset of the range of an existing group G, then the depth of G is incremented and this new group G' has the depth of that group. For example, a group [C:D, depth 1] + [B:E] results in groups [B:E, depth 1] and [C:D, depth 2]. If the requested range is a subset of the range of an existing group G, then the depth of the new group G' becomes one greater than the depth of G. For example, a group [B:E, depth 1] + [C:D] results in groups [B:E, depth 1] and [C:D, depth 2]. If the requested range starts before and ends within, or starts within and ends after, the range of an existing group G, then the range of the existing group G becomes the union of the ranges, and the new group G' has depth one greater than the depth of G and range as the intersection of the ranges. For example, a group [B:D, depth 1] + [C:E] results in groups [B:E, depth 1] and [C:D, depth 2].

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|range|[DimensionRange](#schemadimensionrange)|false|none|The range over which to create a group.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

Adds new cells after the last row with data in a sheet, inserting new rows into the sheet if necessary.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|string(google-fieldmask)|false|none|The fields of CellData that should be updated. At least one field must be specified. The root is the CellData; 'row.values.' should not be specified. A single `"*"` can be used as short-hand for listing every field.|
|rows|[[RowData](#schemarowdata)]|false|none|The data to append.|
|sheetId|integer(int32)|false|none|The sheet ID to append the data to.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|string|false|none|Whether rows or columns should be appended.|
|length|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of rows or columns to append.|
|sheetId|integer(int32)|false|none|The sheet to append rows or columns to.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|dimension|DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED|
|dimension|ROWS|
|dimension|COLUMNS|

Fills in more data based on existing data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range to autofill. This will examine the range and detect the location that has data and automatically fill that data in to the rest of the range.|
|sourceAndDestination|[SourceAndDestination](#schemasourceanddestination)|false|none|The source and destination areas to autofill. This explicitly lists the source of the autofill and where to extend that data.|
|useAlternateSeries|boolean|false|none|True if we should generate data with the "alternate" series. This differs based on the type and amount of source data.|

```json
  }
```


Properties referring a single dimension (either row or column). If both BandedRange.row_properties and BandedRange.column_properties are set, the fill colors are applied to cells according to the following rules: * header_color and footer_color take priority over band colors. * first_band_color takes priority over second_band_color. * row_properties takes priority over column_properties. For example, the first row color takes priority over the first column color, but the first column color takes priority over the second row color. Similarly, the row header takes priority over the column header in the top left cell, but the column header takes priority over the first row color if the row header is not set.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|firstBandColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The first color that is alternating. (Required) Deprecated: Use first_band_color_style.|
|firstBandColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The first color that is alternating. (Required) If first_band_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|
|footerColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The color of the last row or column. If this field is not set, the last row or column is filled with either first_band_color or second_band_color, depending on the color of the previous row or column. Deprecated: Use footer_color_style.|
|footerColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The color of the last row or column. If this field is not set, the last row or column is filled with either first_band_color or second_band_color, depending on the color of the previous row or column. If footer_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|
|headerColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The color of the first row or column. If this field is set, the first row or column is filled with this color and the colors alternate between first_band_color and second_band_color starting from the second row or column. Otherwise, the first row or column is filled with first_band_color and the colors proceed to alternate as they normally would. Deprecated: Use header_color_style.|
|headerColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The color of the first row or column. If this field is set, the first row or column is filled with this color and the colors alternate between first_band_color and second_band_color starting from the second row or column. Otherwise, the first row or column is filled with first_band_color and the colors proceed to alternate as they normally would. If header_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|
|secondBandColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The second color that is alternating. (Required) Deprecated: Use second_band_color_style.|
|secondBandColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The second color that is alternating. (Required) If second_band_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|

A single series of data in a chart. For example, if charting stock prices over time, multiple series may exist, one for the "Open Price", "High Price", "Low Price" and "Close Price".

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|color|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The color for elements (such as bars, lines, and points) associated with this series. If empty, a default color is used. Deprecated: Use color_style.|
|colorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The color for elements (such as bars, lines, and points) associated with this series. If empty, a default color is used. If color is also set, this field takes precedence.|
|dataLabel|[DataLabel](#schemadatalabel)|false|none|Information about the data labels for this series.|
|lineStyle|[LineStyle](#schemalinestyle)|false|none|The line style of this series. Valid only if the chartType is AREA, LINE, or SCATTER. COMBO charts are also supported if the series chart type is AREA or LINE.|
|pointStyle|[PointStyle](#schemapointstyle)|false|none|The style for points associated with this series. Valid only if the chartType is AREA, LINE, or SCATTER. COMBO charts are also supported if the series chart type is AREA, LINE, or SCATTER. If empty, a default point style is used.|
|series|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data being visualized in this chart series.|
|styleOverrides|[[BasicSeriesDataPointStyleOverride](#schemabasicseriesdatapointstyleoverride)]|false|none|Style override settings for series data points.|
|targetAxis|string|false|none|The minor axis that will specify the range of values for this series. For example, if charting stocks over time, the "Volume" series may want to be pinned to the right with the prices pinned to the left, because the scale of trading volume is different than the scale of prices. It is an error to specify an axis that isn't a valid minor axis for the chart's type.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of this series. Valid only if the chartType is COMBO. Different types will change the way the series is visualized. Only LINE, AREA, and COLUMN are supported.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|targetAxis|BASIC_CHART_AXIS_POSITION_UNSPECIFIED|
|targetAxis|BOTTOM_AXIS|
|targetAxis|LEFT_AXIS|
|targetAxis|RIGHT_AXIS|
|type|BASIC_CHART_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|type|BAR|
|type|LINE|
|type|AREA|

The specification for a basic chart. See BasicChartType for the list of charts this supports.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|axis|[[BasicChartAxis](#schemabasicchartaxis)]|false|none|The axis on the chart.|
|chartType|string|false|none|The type of the chart.|
|compareMode|string|false|none|The behavior of tooltips and data highlighting when hovering on data and chart area.|
|domains|[[BasicChartDomain](#schemabasicchartdomain)]|false|none|The domain of data this is charting. Only a single domain is supported.|
|headerCount|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of rows or columns in the data that are "headers". If not set, Google Sheets will guess how many rows are headers based on the data. (Note that BasicChartAxis.title may override the axis title inferred from the header values.)|
|interpolateNulls|boolean|false|none|If some values in a series are missing, gaps may appear in the chart (e.g, segments of lines in a line chart will be missing). To eliminate these gaps set this to true. Applies to Line, Area, and Combo charts.|
|legendPosition|string|false|none|The position of the chart legend.|
|lineSmoothing|boolean|false|none|Gets whether all lines should be rendered smooth or straight by default. Applies to Line charts.|
|series|[[BasicChartSeries](#schemabasicchartseries)]|false|none|The data this chart is visualizing.|
|stackedType|string|false|none|The stacked type for charts that support vertical stacking. Applies to Area, Bar, Column, Combo, and Stepped Area charts.|
|threeDimensional|boolean|false|none|True to make the chart 3D. Applies to Bar and Column charts.|
|totalDataLabel|[DataLabel](#schemadatalabel)|false|none|Controls whether to display additional data labels on stacked charts which sum the total value of all stacked values at each value along the domain axis. These data labels can only be set when chart_type is one of AREA, BAR, COLUMN, COMBO or STEPPED_AREA and stacked_type is either STACKED or PERCENT_STACKED. In addition, for COMBO, this will only be supported if there is only one type of stackable series type or one type has more series than the others and each of the other types have no more than one series. For example, if a chart has two stacked bar series and one area series, the total data labels will be supported. If it has three bar series and two area series, total data labels are not allowed. Neither CUSTOM nor placement can be set on the total_data_label.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|chartType|BASIC_CHART_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|chartType|BAR|
|chartType|LINE|
|chartType|AREA|
|chartType|COLUMN|
|chartType|SCATTER|
|chartType|COMBO|
|chartType|STEPPED_AREA|
|compareMode|BASIC_CHART_COMPARE_MODE_UNSPECIFIED|
|compareMode|DATUM|
|compareMode|CATEGORY|
|legendPosition|BASIC_CHART_LEGEND_POSITION_UNSPECIFIED|
|legendPosition|BOTTOM_LEGEND|
|legendPosition|LEFT_LEGEND|
|legendPosition|RIGHT_LEGEND|
|legendPosition|TOP_LEGEND|
|legendPosition|NO_LEGEND|
|stackedType|BASIC_CHART_STACKED_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|stackedType|NOT_STACKED|
|stackedType|STACKED|
|stackedType|PERCENT_STACKED|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range the filter covers.|
|sortSpecs|[[SortSpec](#schemasortspec)]|false|none|The sort order per column. Later specifications are used when values are equal in the earlier specifications.|

The request for retrieving a range of values in a spreadsheet selected by a set of DataFilters.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dataFilters|[[DataFilter](#schemadatafilter)]|false|none|The data filters used to match the ranges of values to retrieve. Ranges that match any of the specified data filters are included in the response.|
|dateTimeRenderOption|string|false|none|How dates, times, and durations should be represented in the output. This is ignored if value_render_option is FORMATTED_VALUE. The default dateTime render option is SERIAL_NUMBER.|
|majorDimension|string|false|none|The major dimension that results should use. For example, if the spreadsheet data is: `A1=1,B1=2,A2=3,B2=4`, then a request that selects that range and sets `majorDimension=ROWS` returns `[[1,2],[3,4]]`, whereas a request that sets `majorDimension=COLUMNS` returns `[[1,3],[2,4]]`.|
|valueRenderOption|string|false|none|How values should be represented in the output. The default render option is FORMATTED_VALUE.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|dateTimeRenderOption|SERIAL_NUMBER|
|dateTimeRenderOption|FORMATTED_STRING|
|majorDimension|DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED|
|majorDimension|ROWS|
|majorDimension|COLUMNS|
|valueRenderOption|FORMATTED_VALUE|
|valueRenderOption|UNFORMATTED_VALUE|
|valueRenderOption|FORMULA|

The response when retrieving more than one range of values in a spreadsheet selected by DataFilters.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spreadsheetId|string|false|none|The ID of the spreadsheet the data was retrieved from.|
|valueRanges|[[MatchedValueRange](#schemamatchedvaluerange)]|false|none|The requested values with the list of data filters that matched them.|

The response when retrieving more than one range of values in a spreadsheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spreadsheetId|string|false|none|The ID of the spreadsheet the data was retrieved from.|


The request for updating any aspect of a spreadsheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|includeSpreadsheetInResponse|boolean|false|none|Determines if the update response should include the spreadsheet resource.|
|requests|[[Request](#schemarequest)]|false|none|A list of updates to apply to the spreadsheet. Requests will be applied in the order they are specified. If any request is not valid, no requests will be applied.|
|responseIncludeGridData|boolean|false|none|True if grid data should be returned. Meaningful only if include_spreadsheet_in_response is 'true'. This parameter is ignored if a field mask was set in the request.|
|responseRanges|[string]|false|none|Limits the ranges included in the response spreadsheet. Meaningful only if include_spreadsheet_in_response is 'true'.|

The reply for batch updating a spreadsheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|replies|[[Response](#schemaresponse)]|false|none|The reply of the updates. This maps 1:1 with the updates, although replies to some requests may be empty.|
|spreadsheetId|string|false|none|The spreadsheet the updates were applied to.|
|updatedSpreadsheet|[Spreadsheet](#schemaspreadsheet)|false|none|The spreadsheet after updates were applied. This is only set if BatchUpdateSpreadsheetRequest.include_spreadsheet_in_response is `true`.|

The request for updating more than one range of values in a spreadsheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[DataFilterValueRange](#schemadatafiltervaluerange)]|false|none|The new values to apply to the spreadsheet. If more than one range is matched by the specified DataFilter the specified values are applied to all of those ranges.|
|includeValuesInResponse|boolean|false|none|Determines if the update response should include the values of the cells that were updated. By default, responses do not include the updated values. The `updatedData` field within each of the BatchUpdateValuesResponse.responses contains the updated values. If the range to write was larger than the range actually written, the response includes all values in the requested range (excluding trailing empty rows and columns).|
|responseDateTimeRenderOption|string|false|none|Determines how dates, times, and durations in the response should be rendered. This is ignored if response_value_render_option is FORMATTED_VALUE. The default dateTime render option is SERIAL_NUMBER.|
|responseValueRenderOption|string|false|none|Determines how values in the response should be rendered. The default render option is FORMATTED_VALUE.|
|valueInputOption|string|false|none|How the input data should be interpreted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|responseDateTimeRenderOption|SERIAL_NUMBER|
|responseDateTimeRenderOption|FORMATTED_STRING|
|responseValueRenderOption|FORMATTED_VALUE|
|responseValueRenderOption|UNFORMATTED_VALUE|
|responseValueRenderOption|FORMULA|
|valueInputOption|INPUT_VALUE_OPTION_UNSPECIFIED|
|valueInputOption|RAW|
|valueInputOption|USER_ENTERED|

```json
  "responseDateTimeRenderOption": "SERIAL_NUMBER",
  "responseValueRenderOption": "FORMATTED_VALUE",
  "valueInputOption": "INPUT_VALUE_OPTION_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

The request for updating more than one range of values in a spreadsheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[ValueRange](#schemavaluerange)]|false|none|The new values to apply to the spreadsheet.|
|includeValuesInResponse|boolean|false|none|Determines if the update response should include the values of the cells that were updated. By default, responses do not include the updated values. The `updatedData` field within each of the BatchUpdateValuesResponse.responses contains the updated values. If the range to write was larger than the range actually written, the response includes all values in the requested range (excluding trailing empty rows and columns).|
|responseDateTimeRenderOption|string|false|none|Determines how dates, times, and durations in the response should be rendered. This is ignored if response_value_render_option is FORMATTED_VALUE. The default dateTime render option is SERIAL_NUMBER.|
|responseValueRenderOption|string|false|none|Determines how values in the response should be rendered. The default render option is FORMATTED_VALUE.|
|valueInputOption|string|false|none|How the input data should be interpreted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|responseDateTimeRenderOption|SERIAL_NUMBER|
|responseDateTimeRenderOption|FORMATTED_STRING|
|responseValueRenderOption|FORMATTED_VALUE|
|responseValueRenderOption|UNFORMATTED_VALUE|
|responseValueRenderOption|FORMULA|
|valueInputOption|INPUT_VALUE_OPTION_UNSPECIFIED|
|valueInputOption|RAW|
|valueInputOption|USER_ENTERED|

|bubbleMinRadiusSize|integer(int32)|false|none|The minimum radius size of the bubbles, in pixels. If specific, the field must be a positive value.|

|domain|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data containing the bubble x-values. These values locate the bubbles in the chart horizontally.|
|groupIds|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data containing the bubble group IDs. All bubbles with the same group ID are drawn in the same color. If bubble_sizes is specified then this field must also be specified but may contain blank values. This field is optional.|

|series|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data containing the bubble y-values. These values locate the bubbles in the chart vertically.|

The Candlestick chart data, each containing the low, open, close, and high values for a series.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|closeSeries|[CandlestickSeries](#schemacandlestickseries)|false|none|The range data (vertical axis) for the close/final value for each candle. This is the top of the candle body. If greater than the open value the candle will be filled. Otherwise the candle will be hollow.|
|highSeries|[CandlestickSeries](#schemacandlestickseries)|false|none|The range data (vertical axis) for the high/maximum value for each candle. This is the top of the candle's center line.|
|lowSeries|[CandlestickSeries](#schemacandlestickseries)|false|none|The range data (vertical axis) for the low/minimum value for each candle. This is the bottom of the candle's center line.|
|openSeries|[CandlestickSeries](#schemacandlestickseries)|false|none|The range data (vertical axis) for the open/initial value for each candle. This is the bottom of the candle body. If less than the close value the candle will be filled. Otherwise the candle will be hollow.|

Data about a specific cell.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dataSourceFormula|[DataSourceFormula](#schemadatasourceformula)|false|none|Output only. Information about a data source formula on the cell. The field is set if user_entered_value is a formula referencing some DATA_SOURCE sheet, e.g. `=SUM(DataSheet!Column)`.|
|dataSourceTable|[DataSourceTable](#schemadatasourcetable)|false|none|A data source table anchored at this cell. The size of data source table itself is computed dynamically based on its configuration. Only the first cell of the data source table contains the data source table definition. The other cells will contain the display values of the data source table result in their effective_value fields.|
|dataValidation|[DataValidationRule](#schemadatavalidationrule)|false|none|A data validation rule on the cell, if any. When writing, the new data validation rule will overwrite any prior rule.|
|effectiveFormat|[CellFormat](#schemacellformat)|false|none|The effective format being used by the cell. This includes the results of applying any conditional formatting and, if the cell contains a formula, the computed number format. If the effective format is the default format, effective format will not be written. This field is read-only.|
|effectiveValue|[ExtendedValue](#schemaextendedvalue)|false|none|The effective value of the cell. For cells with formulas, this is the calculated value. For cells with literals, this is the same as the user_entered_value. This field is read-only.|
|formattedValue|string|false|none|The formatted value of the cell. This is the value as it's shown to the user. This field is read-only.|
|hyperlink|string|false|none|A hyperlink this cell points to, if any. If the cell contains multiple hyperlinks, this field will be empty. This field is read-only. To set it, use a `=HYPERLINK` formula in the userEnteredValue.formulaValue field. A cell-level link can also be set from the userEnteredFormat.textFormat field. Alternatively, set a hyperlink in the textFormatRun.format.link field that spans the entire cell.|
|note|string|false|none|Any note on the cell.|
|pivotTable|[PivotTable](#schemapivottable)|false|none|A pivot table anchored at this cell. The size of pivot table itself is computed dynamically based on its data, grouping, filters, values, etc. Only the top-left cell of the pivot table contains the pivot table definition. The other cells will contain the calculated values of the results of the pivot in their effective_value fields.|
|textFormatRuns|[[TextFormatRun](#schematextformatrun)]|false|none|Runs of rich text applied to subsections of the cell. Runs are only valid on user entered strings, not formulas, bools, or numbers. Properties of a run start at a specific index in the text and continue until the next run. Runs will inherit the properties of the cell unless explicitly changed. When writing, the new runs will overwrite any prior runs. When writing a new user_entered_value, previous runs are erased.|
|userEnteredFormat|[CellFormat](#schemacellformat)|false|none|The format the user entered for the cell. When writing, the new format will be merged with the existing format.|
|userEnteredValue|[ExtendedValue](#schemaextendedvalue)|false|none|The value the user entered in the cell. e.g., `1234`, `'Hello'`, or `=NOW()` Note: Dates, Times and DateTimes are represented as doubles in serial number format.|

```json
  "dateTimeRule": {
    "type": "CHART_DATE_TIME_RULE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
  },
  "histogramRule": {
    "intervalSize": 0,
    "maxValue": 0,
    "minValue": 0
  }
}
```

An optional setting on the ChartData of the domain of a data source chart that defines buckets for the values in the domain rather than breaking out each individual value. For example, when plotting a data source chart, you can specify a histogram rule on the domain (it should only contain numeric values), grouping its values into buckets. Any values of a chart series that fall into the same bucket are aggregated based on the aggregate_type.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dateTimeRule|[ChartDateTimeRule](#schemachartdatetimerule)|false|none|A ChartDateTimeRule.|
|histogramRule|[ChartHistogramRule](#schemacharthistogramrule)|false|none|A ChartHistogramRule|

<h2 id="tocS_ChartHistogramRule">ChartHistogramRule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacharthistogramrule"></a>
<a id="schema_ChartHistogramRule"></a>
<a id="tocScharthistogramrule"></a>
<a id="tocscharthistogramrule"></a>

```json
{
  "intervalSize": 0,
  "maxValue": 0,
  "minValue": 0
}
```

Allows you to organize numeric values in a source data column into buckets of constant size.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intervalSize|number(double)|false|none|The size of the buckets that are created. Must be positive.|
|maxValue|number(double)|false|none|The maximum value at which items are placed into buckets. Values greater than the maximum are grouped into a single bucket. If omitted, it is determined by the maximum item value.|
|minValue|number(double)|false|none|The minimum value at which items are placed into buckets. Values that are less than the minimum are grouped into a single bucket. If omitted, it is determined by the minimum item value.|

```json
{
  "sources": [

      "endColumnIndex": 0,
      "endRowIndex": 0,

      "startColumnIndex": 0,

    }
  ]
}
```

Source ranges for a chart.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sources|[[GridRange](#schemagridrange)]|false|none|The ranges of data for a series or domain. Exactly one dimension must have a length of 1, and all sources in the list must have the same dimension with length 1. The domain (if it exists) & all series must have the same number of source ranges. If using more than one source range, then the source range at a given offset must be in order and contiguous across the domain and series. For example, these are valid configurations: domain sources: A1:A5 series1 sources: B1:B5 series2 sources: D6:D10 domain sources: A1:A5, C10:C12 series1 sources: B1:B5, D10:D12 series2 sources: C1:C5, E10:E12|

The specifications of a chart.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|altText|string|false|none|The alternative text that describes the chart. This is often used for accessibility.|
|backgroundColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The background color of the entire chart. Not applicable to Org charts. Deprecated: Use background_color_style.|
|backgroundColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The background color of the entire chart. Not applicable to Org charts. If background_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|
|basicChart|[BasicChartSpec](#schemabasicchartspec)|false|none|A basic chart specification, can be one of many kinds of charts. See BasicChartType for the list of all charts this supports.|
|bubbleChart|[BubbleChartSpec](#schemabubblechartspec)|false|none|A bubble chart specification.|
|candlestickChart|[CandlestickChartSpec](#schemacandlestickchartspec)|false|none|A candlestick chart specification.|
|dataSourceChartProperties|[DataSourceChartProperties](#schemadatasourcechartproperties)|false|none|If present, the field contains data source chart specific properties.|
|filterSpecs|[[FilterSpec](#schemafilterspec)]|false|none|The filters applied to the source data of the chart. Only supported for data source charts.|
|fontName|string|false|none|The name of the font to use by default for all chart text (e.g. title, axis labels, legend). If a font is specified for a specific part of the chart it will override this font name.|
|hiddenDimensionStrategy|string|false|none|Determines how the charts will use hidden rows or columns.|
|histogramChart|[HistogramChartSpec](#schemahistogramchartspec)|false|none|A histogram chart specification.|
|maximized|boolean|false|none|True to make a chart fill the entire space in which it's rendered with minimum padding. False to use the default padding. (Not applicable to Geo and Org charts.)|
|orgChart|[OrgChartSpec](#schemaorgchartspec)|false|none|An org chart specification.|
|pieChart|[PieChartSpec](#schemapiechartspec)|false|none|A pie chart specification.|
|scorecardChart|[ScorecardChartSpec](#schemascorecardchartspec)|false|none|A scorecard chart specification.|
|sortSpecs|[[SortSpec](#schemasortspec)]|false|none|The order to sort the chart data by. Only a single sort spec is supported. Only supported for data source charts.|
|subtitle|string|false|none|The subtitle of the chart.|
|subtitleTextFormat|[TextFormat](#schematextformat)|false|none|The subtitle text format. Strikethrough, underline, and link are not supported.|
|subtitleTextPosition|[TextPosition](#schematextposition)|false|none|The subtitle text position. This field is optional.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the chart.|
|titleTextFormat|[TextFormat](#schematextformat)|false|none|The title text format. Strikethrough, underline, and link are not supported.|
|titleTextPosition|[TextPosition](#schematextposition)|false|none|The title text position. This field is optional.|
|treemapChart|[TreemapChartSpec](#schematreemapchartspec)|false|none|A treemap chart specification.|
|waterfallChart|[WaterfallChartSpec](#schemawaterfallchartspec)|false|none|A waterfall chart specification.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

|hiddenDimensionStrategy|CHART_HIDDEN_DIMENSION_STRATEGY_UNSPECIFIED|
|hiddenDimensionStrategy|SKIP_HIDDEN_ROWS_AND_COLUMNS|
|hiddenDimensionStrategy|SKIP_HIDDEN_ROWS|
|hiddenDimensionStrategy|SKIP_HIDDEN_COLUMNS|
|hiddenDimensionStrategy|SHOW_ALL|

<h2 id="tocS_Color">Color</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacolor"></a>
<a id="schema_Color"></a>
<a id="tocScolor"></a>
<a id="tocscolor"></a>

```json
{
  "alpha": 0,
  "blue": 0,
  "green": 0,
  "red": 0
}
```

Represents a color in the RGBA color space. This representation is designed for simplicity of conversion to and from color representations in various languages over compactness. For example, the fields of this representation can be trivially provided to the constructor of `java.awt.Color` in Java; it can also be trivially provided to UIColor's `+colorWithRed:green:blue:alpha` method in iOS; and, with just a little work, it can be easily formatted into a CSS `rgba()` string in JavaScript. This reference page doesn't have information about the absolute color space that should be used to interpret the RGB value—for example, sRGB, Adobe RGB, DCI-P3, and BT.2020. By default, applications should assume the sRGB color space. When color equality needs to be decided, implementations, unless documented otherwise, treat two colors as equal if all their red, green, blue, and alpha values each differ by at most `1e-5`. Example (Java): import com.google.type.Color; // ... public static java.awt.Color fromProto(Color protocolor) { float alpha = protocolor.hasAlpha() ? protocolor.getAlpha().getValue() : 1.0; return new java.awt.Color( protocolor.getRed(), protocolor.getGreen(), protocolor.getBlue(), alpha); } public static Color toProto(java.awt.Color color) { float red = (float) color.getRed(); float green = (float) color.getGreen(); float blue = (float) color.getBlue(); float denominator = 255.0; Color.Builder resultBuilder = Color .newBuilder() .setRed(red / denominator) .setGreen(green / denominator) .setBlue(blue / denominator); int alpha = color.getAlpha(); if (alpha != 255) { result.setAlpha( FloatValue .newBuilder() .setValue(((float) alpha) / denominator) .build()); } return resultBuilder.build(); } // ... Example (iOS / Obj-C): // ... static UIColor* fromProto(Color* protocolor) { float red = [protocolor red]; float green = [protocolor green]; float blue = [protocolor blue]; FloatValue* alpha_wrapper = [protocolor alpha]; float alpha = 1.0; if (alpha_wrapper != nil) { alpha = [alpha_wrapper value]; } return [UIColor colorWithRed:red green:green blue:blue alpha:alpha]; } static Color* toProto(UIColor* color) { CGFloat red, green, blue, alpha; if (![color getRed:&red green:&green blue:&blue alpha:&alpha]) { return nil; } Color* result = [[Color alloc] init]; [result setRed:red]; [result setGreen:green]; [result setBlue:blue]; if (alpha <= 0.9999) { [result setAlpha:floatWrapperWithValue(alpha)]; } [result autorelease]; return result; } // ... Example (JavaScript): // ... var protoToCssColor = function(rgb_color) { var redFrac = rgb_color.red || 0.0; var greenFrac = rgb_color.green || 0.0; var blueFrac = rgb_color.blue || 0.0; var red = Math.floor(redFrac * 255); var green = Math.floor(greenFrac * 255); var blue = Math.floor(blueFrac * 255); if (!('alpha' in rgb_color)) { return rgbToCssColor(red, green, blue); } var alphaFrac = rgb_color.alpha.value || 0.0; var rgbParams = [red, green, blue].join(','); return ['rgba(', rgbParams, ',', alphaFrac, ')'].join(''); }; var rgbToCssColor = function(red, green, blue) { var rgbNumber = new Number((red << 16) | (green << 8) | blue); var hexString = rgbNumber.toString(16); var missingZeros = 6 - hexString.length; var resultBuilder = ['#']; for (var i = 0; i < missingZeros; i++) { resultBuilder.push('0'); } resultBuilder.push(hexString); return resultBuilder.join(''); }; // ...

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alpha|number(float)|false|none|The fraction of this color that should be applied to the pixel. That is, the final pixel color is defined by the equation: `pixel color = alpha * (this color) + (1.0 - alpha) * (background color)` This means that a value of 1.0 corresponds to a solid color, whereas a value of 0.0 corresponds to a completely transparent color. This uses a wrapper message rather than a simple float scalar so that it is possible to distinguish between a default value and the value being unset. If omitted, this color object is rendered as a solid color (as if the alpha value had been explicitly given a value of 1.0).|
|blue|number(float)|false|none|The amount of blue in the color as a value in the interval [0, 1].|
|green|number(float)|false|none|The amount of green in the color as a value in the interval [0, 1].|
|red|number(float)|false|none|The amount of red in the color as a value in the interval [0, 1].|

<h2 id="tocS_DataExecutionStatus">DataExecutionStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadataexecutionstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_DataExecutionStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSdataexecutionstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsdataexecutionstatus"></a>

```json
{
  "errorCode": "DATA_EXECUTION_ERROR_CODE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "errorMessage": "string",
  "lastRefreshTime": "string",
  "state": "DATA_EXECUTION_STATE_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

The data execution status. A data execution is created to sync a data source object with the latest data from a DataSource. It is usually scheduled to run at background, you can check its state to tell if an execution completes There are several scenarios where a data execution is triggered to run: * Adding a data source creates an associated data source sheet as well as a data execution to sync the data from the data source to the sheet. * Updating a data source creates a data execution to refresh the associated data source sheet similarly. * You can send refresh request to explicitly refresh one or multiple data source objects.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errorCode|string|false|none|The error code.|
|errorMessage|string|false|none|The error message, which may be empty.|
|lastRefreshTime|string(google-datetime)|false|none|Gets the time the data last successfully refreshed.|
|state|string|false|none|The state of the data execution.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|errorCode|DATA_EXECUTION_ERROR_CODE_UNSPECIFIED|
|errorCode|TIMED_OUT|
|errorCode|TOO_MANY_ROWS|
|errorCode|TOO_MANY_COLUMNS|
|errorCode|TOO_MANY_CELLS|
|errorCode|ENGINE|
|errorCode|PARAMETER_INVALID|
|errorCode|UNSUPPORTED_DATA_TYPE|
|errorCode|DUPLICATE_COLUMN_NAMES|
|errorCode|INTERRUPTED|
|errorCode|CONCURRENT_QUERY|
|errorCode|OTHER|
|errorCode|TOO_MANY_CHARS_PER_CELL|
|errorCode|DATA_NOT_FOUND|
|errorCode|PERMISSION_DENIED|
|errorCode|MISSING_COLUMN_ALIAS|
|errorCode|OBJECT_NOT_FOUND|
|errorCode|OBJECT_IN_ERROR_STATE|
|errorCode|OBJECT_SPEC_INVALID|
|state|DATA_EXECUTION_STATE_UNSPECIFIED|
|state|NOT_STARTED|
|state|RUNNING|
|state|SUCCEEDED|
|state|FAILED|

Settings for one set of data labels. Data labels are annotations that appear next to a set of data, such as the points on a line chart, and provide additional information about what the data represents, such as a text representation of the value behind that point on the graph.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customLabelData|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|Data to use for custom labels. Only used if type is set to CUSTOM. This data must be the same length as the series or other element this data label is applied to. In addition, if the series is split into multiple source ranges, this source data must come from the next column in the source data. For example, if the series is B2:B4,E6:E8 then this data must come from C2:C4,F6:F8.|
|placement|string|false|none|The placement of the data label relative to the labeled data.|
|textFormat|[TextFormat](#schematextformat)|false|none|The text format used for the data label. The link field is not supported.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the data label.|

|placement|OUTSIDE_END|

|type|DATA|
|type|CUSTOM|

<a id="tocSdatasourceparameter"></a>
<a id="tocsdatasourceparameter"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "namedRangeId": "string",
  "range": {
    "endColumnIndex": 0,
    "endRowIndex": 0,
    "sheetId": 0,
    "startColumnIndex": 0,
    "startRowIndex": 0
  }
}
```

A parameter in a data source's query. The parameter allows the user to pass in values from the spreadsheet into a query.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Named parameter. Must be a legitimate identifier for the DataSource that supports it. For example, [BigQuery identifier](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/lexical#identifiers).|
|namedRangeId|string|false|none|ID of a NamedRange. Its size must be 1x1.|
|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|A range that contains the value of the parameter. Its size must be 1x1.|

A schedule for data to refresh every day in a given time interval.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startTime|[TimeOfDay](#schematimeofday)|false|none|The start time of a time interval in which a data source refresh is scheduled. Only `hours` part is used. The time interval size defaults to that in the Sheets editor.|

<h2 id="tocS_DataSourceRefreshMonthlySchedule">DataSourceRefreshMonthlySchedule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json

  "daysOfMonth": [
    0
  ],
  "startTime": {
    "hours": 0,
    "minutes": 0,
    "nanos": 0,
    "seconds": 0
  }
}
```

A monthly schedule for data to refresh on specific days in the month in a given time interval.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|daysOfMonth|[integer(int32)]|false|none|Days of the month to refresh. Only 1-28 are supported, mapping to the 1st to the 28th day. At least one day must be specified.|
|startTime|[TimeOfDay](#schematimeofday)|false|none|The start time of a time interval in which a data source refresh is scheduled. Only `hours` part is used. The time interval size defaults to that in the Sheets editor.|

<h2 id="tocS_DataSourceRefreshSchedule">DataSourceRefreshSchedule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadatasourcerefreshschedule"></a>
<a id="schema_DataSourceRefreshSchedule"></a>
<a id="tocSdatasourcerefreshschedule"></a>
<a id="tocsdatasourcerefreshschedule"></a>

```json
{
  "dailySchedule": {
    "startTime": {
      "hours": 0,
      "minutes": 0,
      "nanos": 0,
      "seconds": 0
    }
  },
  "enabled": true,
  "monthlySchedule": {
    "daysOfMonth": [
      0
    ],
    "startTime": {
      "hours": 0,
      "minutes": 0,
      "nanos": 0,
      "seconds": 0
    }
  },
  "nextRun": {
    "endTime": "string",
    "startTime": "string"
  },
  "refreshScope": "DATA_SOURCE_REFRESH_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "weeklySchedule": {
    "daysOfWeek": [
      "DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED"
    ],
    "startTime": {
      "hours": 0,
      "minutes": 0,
      "nanos": 0,
      "seconds": 0
    }
  }
}
```

Schedule for refreshing the data source. Data sources in the spreadsheet are refreshed within a time interval. You can specify the start time by clicking the Scheduled Refresh button in the Sheets editor, but the interval is fixed at 4 hours. For example, if you specify a start time of 8 AM , the refresh will take place between 8 AM and 12 PM every day.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dailySchedule|[DataSourceRefreshDailySchedule](#schemadatasourcerefreshdailyschedule)|false|none|Daily refresh schedule.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|True if the refresh schedule is enabled, or false otherwise.|
|monthlySchedule|[DataSourceRefreshMonthlySchedule](#schemadatasourcerefreshmonthlyschedule)|false|none|Monthly refresh schedule.|
|nextRun|[Interval](#schemainterval)|false|none|Output only. The time interval of the next run.|
|refreshScope|string|false|none|The scope of the refresh. Must be ALL_DATA_SOURCES.|
|weeklySchedule|[DataSourceRefreshWeeklySchedule](#schemadatasourcerefreshweeklyschedule)|false|none|Weekly refresh schedule.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|refreshScope|DATA_SOURCE_REFRESH_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|refreshScope|ALL_DATA_SOURCES|

A data source table, which allows the user to import a static table of data from the DataSource into Sheets. This is also known as "Extract" in the Sheets editor.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|columnSelectionType|string|false|none|The type to select columns for the data source table. Defaults to SELECTED.|
|columns|[[DataSourceColumnReference](#schemadatasourcecolumnreference)]|false|none|Columns selected for the data source table. The column_selection_type must be SELECTED.|
|dataExecutionStatus|[DataExecutionStatus](#schemadataexecutionstatus)|false|none|Output only. The data execution status.|
|dataSourceId|string|false|none|The ID of the data source the data source table is associated with.|
|filterSpecs|[[FilterSpec](#schemafilterspec)]|false|none|Filter specifications in the data source table.|
|rowLimit|integer(int32)|false|none|The limit of rows to return. If not set, a default limit is applied. Please refer to the Sheets editor for the default and max limit.|
|sortSpecs|[[SortSpec](#schemasortspec)]|false|none|Sort specifications in the data source table. The result of the data source table is sorted based on the sort specifications in order.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|columnSelectionType|DATA_SOURCE_TABLE_COLUMN_SELECTION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|columnSelectionType|SELECTED|
|columnSelectionType|SYNC_ALL|

<h2 id="tocS_DateTimeRule">DateTimeRule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadatetimerule"></a>
<a id="schema_DateTimeRule"></a>
<a id="tocSdatetimerule"></a>
<a id="tocsdatetimerule"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "DATE_TIME_RULE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

Allows you to organize the date-time values in a source data column into buckets based on selected parts of their date or time values. For example, consider a pivot table showing sales transactions by date: +----------+--------------+ | Date | SUM of Sales | +----------+--------------+ | 1/1/2017 | $621.14 | | 2/3/2017 | $708.84 | | 5/8/2017 | $326.84 | ... +----------+--------------+ Applying a date-time group rule with a DateTimeRuleType of YEAR_MONTH results in the following pivot table. +--------------+--------------+ | Grouped Date | SUM of Sales | +--------------+--------------+ | 2017-Jan | $53,731.78 | | 2017-Feb | $83,475.32 | | 2017-Mar | $94,385.05 | ... +--------------+--------------+

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of date-time grouping to apply.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|DATE_TIME_RULE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|type|SECOND|
|type|MINUTE|
|type|HOUR|
|type|HOUR_MINUTE|
|type|HOUR_MINUTE_AMPM|
|type|DAY_OF_WEEK|
|type|DAY_OF_YEAR|
|type|DAY_OF_MONTH|
|type|DAY_MONTH|
|type|MONTH|
|type|QUARTER|
|type|YEAR|
|type|YEAR_MONTH|
|type|YEAR_QUARTER|
|type|YEAR_MONTH_DAY|

<h2 id="tocS_DeleteDuplicatesRequest">DeleteDuplicatesRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadeleteduplicatesrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_DeleteDuplicatesRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSdeleteduplicatesrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsdeleteduplicatesrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "comparisonColumns": [
    {
      "dimension": "DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED",
      "endIndex": 0,
      "sheetId": 0,
      "startIndex": 0
    }
  ],
  "range": {
    "endColumnIndex": 0,
    "endRowIndex": 0,
    "sheetId": 0,
    "startColumnIndex": 0,
    "startRowIndex": 0
  }
}
```

Removes rows within this range that contain values in the specified columns that are duplicates of values in any previous row. Rows with identical values but different letter cases, formatting, or formulas are considered to be duplicates. This request also removes duplicate rows hidden from view (for example, due to a filter). When removing duplicates, the first instance of each duplicate row scanning from the top downwards is kept in the resulting range. Content outside of the specified range isn't removed, and rows considered duplicates do not have to be adjacent to each other in the range.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comparisonColumns|[[DimensionRange](#schemadimensionrange)]|false|none|The columns in the range to analyze for duplicate values. If no columns are selected then all columns are analyzed for duplicates.|
|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range to remove duplicates rows from.|

<h2 id="tocS_DeveloperMetadata">DeveloperMetadata</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadevelopermetadata"></a>
<a id="schema_DeveloperMetadata"></a>
<a id="tocSdevelopermetadata"></a>
<a id="tocsdevelopermetadata"></a>

```json
{
  "location": {
    "dimensionRange": {
      "dimension": "DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED",
      "endIndex": 0,
      "sheetId": 0,
      "startIndex": 0
    },
    "locationType": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_LOCATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
    "sheetId": 0,
    "spreadsheet": true
  },
  "metadataId": 0,
  "metadataKey": "string",
  "metadataValue": "string",
  "visibility": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_VISIBILITY_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

Developer metadata associated with a location or object in a spreadsheet. Developer metadata may be used to associate arbitrary data with various parts of a spreadsheet and will remain associated at those locations as they move around and the spreadsheet is edited. For example, if developer metadata is associated with row 5 and another row is then subsequently inserted above row 5, that original metadata will still be associated with the row it was first associated with (what is now row 6). If the associated object is deleted its metadata is deleted too.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|location|[DeveloperMetadataLocation](#schemadevelopermetadatalocation)|false|none|The location where the metadata is associated.|
|metadataId|integer(int32)|false|none|The spreadsheet-scoped unique ID that identifies the metadata. IDs may be specified when metadata is created, otherwise one will be randomly generated and assigned. Must be positive.|
|metadataKey|string|false|none|The metadata key. There may be multiple metadata in a spreadsheet with the same key. Developer metadata must always have a key specified.|
|metadataValue|string|false|none|Data associated with the metadata's key.|
|visibility|string|false|none|The metadata visibility. Developer metadata must always have a visibility specified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|visibility|DEVELOPER_METADATA_VISIBILITY_UNSPECIFIED|
|visibility|DOCUMENT|
|visibility|PROJECT|

<h2 id="tocS_DeveloperMetadataLookup">DeveloperMetadataLookup</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadevelopermetadatalookup"></a>
<a id="schema_DeveloperMetadataLookup"></a>
<a id="tocSdevelopermetadatalookup"></a>
<a id="tocsdevelopermetadatalookup"></a>

```json
{
  "locationMatchingStrategy": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_LOCATION_MATCHING_STRATEGY_UNSPECIFIED",
  "locationType": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_LOCATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "metadataId": 0,
  "metadataKey": "string",
  "metadataLocation": {
    "dimensionRange": {
      "dimension": "DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED",
      "endIndex": 0,
      "sheetId": 0,
      "startIndex": 0
    },
    "locationType": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_LOCATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
    "sheetId": 0,
    "spreadsheet": true
  },
  "metadataValue": "string",
  "visibility": "DEVELOPER_METADATA_VISIBILITY_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

Selects DeveloperMetadata that matches all of the specified fields. For example, if only a metadata ID is specified this considers the DeveloperMetadata with that particular unique ID. If a metadata key is specified, this considers all developer metadata with that key. If a key, visibility, and location type are all specified, this considers all developer metadata with that key and visibility that are associated with a location of that type. In general, this selects all DeveloperMetadata that matches the intersection of all the specified fields; any field or combination of fields may be specified.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|locationMatchingStrategy|string|false|none|Determines how this lookup matches the location. If this field is specified as EXACT, only developer metadata associated on the exact location specified is matched. If this field is specified to INTERSECTING, developer metadata associated on intersecting locations is also matched. If left unspecified, this field assumes a default value of INTERSECTING. If this field is specified, a metadataLocation must also be specified.|
|locationType|string|false|none|Limits the selected developer metadata to those entries which are associated with locations of the specified type. For example, when this field is specified as ROW this lookup only considers developer metadata associated on rows. If the field is left unspecified, all location types are considered. This field cannot be specified as SPREADSHEET when the locationMatchingStrategy is specified as INTERSECTING or when the metadataLocation is specified as a non-spreadsheet location: spreadsheet metadata cannot intersect any other developer metadata location. This field also must be left unspecified when the locationMatchingStrategy is specified as EXACT.|
|metadataId|integer(int32)|false|none|Limits the selected developer metadata to that which has a matching DeveloperMetadata.metadata_id.|
|metadataKey|string|false|none|Limits the selected developer metadata to that which has a matching DeveloperMetadata.metadata_key.|
|metadataLocation|[DeveloperMetadataLocation](#schemadevelopermetadatalocation)|false|none|Limits the selected developer metadata to those entries associated with the specified location. This field either matches exact locations or all intersecting locations according the specified locationMatchingStrategy.|
|metadataValue|string|false|none|Limits the selected developer metadata to that which has a matching DeveloperMetadata.metadata_value.|
|visibility|string|false|none|Limits the selected developer metadata to that which has a matching DeveloperMetadata.visibility. If left unspecified, all developer metadata visibile to the requesting project is considered.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|locationMatchingStrategy|DEVELOPER_METADATA_LOCATION_MATCHING_STRATEGY_UNSPECIFIED|
|locationMatchingStrategy|EXACT_LOCATION|
|locationMatchingStrategy|INTERSECTING_LOCATION|
|locationType|DEVELOPER_METADATA_LOCATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|locationType|ROW|
|locationType|COLUMN|
|locationType|SHEET|
|locationType|SPREADSHEET|
|visibility|DEVELOPER_METADATA_VISIBILITY_UNSPECIFIED|
|visibility|DOCUMENT|
|visibility|PROJECT|

```json
    "dimension": "DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED",
    "endIndex": 0,
    "sheetId": 0,
    "startIndex": 0
  }
}
```

A group over an interval of rows or columns on a sheet, which can contain or be contained within other groups. A group can be collapsed or expanded as a unit on the sheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collapsed|boolean|false|none|This field is true if this group is collapsed. A collapsed group remains collapsed if an overlapping group at a shallower depth is expanded. A true value does not imply that all dimensions within the group are hidden, since a dimension's visibility can change independently from this group property. However, when this property is updated, all dimensions within it are set to hidden if this field is true, or set to visible if this field is false.|
|depth|integer(int32)|false|none|The depth of the group, representing how many groups have a range that wholly contains the range of this group.|
|range|[DimensionRange](#schemadimensionrange)|false|none|The range over which this group exists.|

<h2 id="tocS_DuplicateSheetRequest">DuplicateSheetRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaduplicatesheetrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_DuplicateSheetRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSduplicatesheetrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsduplicatesheetrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "insertSheetIndex": 0,
  "newSheetId": 0,
  "newSheetName": "string",
  "sourceSheetId": 0
}
```

Duplicates the contents of a sheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|insertSheetIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The zero-based index where the new sheet should be inserted. The index of all sheets after this are incremented.|
|newSheetId|integer(int32)|false|none|If set, the ID of the new sheet. If not set, an ID is chosen. If set, the ID must not conflict with any existing sheet ID. If set, it must be non-negative.|
|newSheetName|string|false|none|The name of the new sheet. If empty, a new name is chosen for you.|
|sourceSheetId|integer(int32)|false|none|The sheet to duplicate. If the source sheet is of DATA_SOURCE type, its backing DataSource is also duplicated and associated with the new copy of the sheet. No data execution is triggered, the grid data of this sheet is also copied over but only available after the batch request completes.|

```json
  ]

```

The editors of a protected range.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domainUsersCanEdit|boolean|false|none|True if anyone in the document's domain has edit access to the protected range. Domain protection is only supported on documents within a domain.|
|groups|[string]|false|none|The email addresses of groups with edit access to the protected range.|
|users|[string]|false|none|The email addresses of users with edit access to the protected range.|

A chart embedded in a sheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|border|[EmbeddedObjectBorder](#schemaembeddedobjectborder)|false|none|The border of the chart.|
|chartId|integer(int32)|false|none|The ID of the chart.|
|position|[EmbeddedObjectPosition](#schemaembeddedobjectposition)|false|none|The position of the chart.|
|spec|[ChartSpec](#schemachartspec)|false|none|The specification of the chart.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|newSheet|boolean|false|none|If true, the embedded object is put on a new sheet whose ID is chosen for you. Used only when writing.|
|overlayPosition|[OverlayPosition](#schemaoverlayposition)|false|none|The position at which the object is overlaid on top of a grid.|
|sheetId|integer(int32)|false|none|The sheet this is on. Set only if the embedded object is on its own sheet. Must be non-negative.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boolValue|boolean|false|none|Represents a boolean value.|

|formulaValue|string|false|none|Represents a formula.|

|visibleForegroundColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The foreground color to filter by; only cells with this foreground color are shown. Mutually exclusive with visible_background_color. Deprecated: Use visible_foreground_color_style.|
|visibleForegroundColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The foreground color to filter by; only cells with this foreground color are shown. This field is mutually exclusive with visible_background_color, and must be set to an RGB-type color. If visible_foreground_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|

<h2 id="tocS_FindReplaceRequest">FindReplaceRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafindreplacerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_FindReplaceRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSfindreplacerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsfindreplacerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "allSheets": true,
  "find": "string",
  "includeFormulas": true,
  "matchCase": true,
  "matchEntireCell": true,
  "range": {
    "endColumnIndex": 0,
    "endRowIndex": 0,
    "sheetId": 0,
    "startColumnIndex": 0,
    "startRowIndex": 0
  },
  "replacement": "string",
  "searchByRegex": true,
  "sheetId": 0
}
```

Finds and replaces data in cells over a range, sheet, or all sheets.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allSheets|boolean|false|none|True to find/replace over all sheets.|
|find|string|false|none|The value to search.|
|includeFormulas|boolean|false|none|True if the search should include cells with formulas. False to skip cells with formulas.|
|matchCase|boolean|false|none|True if the search is case sensitive.|
|matchEntireCell|boolean|false|none|True if the find value should match the entire cell.|
|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range to find/replace over.|
|replacement|string|false|none|The value to use as the replacement.|
|searchByRegex|boolean|false|none|True if the find value is a regex. The regular expression and replacement should follow Java regex rules at https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/regex/Pattern.html. The replacement string is allowed to refer to capturing groups. For example, if one cell has the contents `"Google Sheets"` and another has `"Google Docs"`, then searching for `"o.* (.*)"` with a replacement of `"$1 Rocks"` would change the contents of the cells to `"GSheets Rocks"` and `"GDocs Rocks"` respectively.|
|sheetId|integer(int32)|false|none|The sheet to find/replace over.|

```json
{
  "formulasChanged": 0,
  "occurrencesChanged": 0,
  "rowsChanged": 0,
  "sheetsChanged": 0,
  "valuesChanged": 0
}
```

The result of the find/replace.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|formulasChanged|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of formula cells changed.|
|occurrencesChanged|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of occurrences (possibly multiple within a cell) changed. For example, if replacing `"e"` with `"o"` in `"Google Sheets"`, this would be `"3"` because `"Google Sheets"` -> `"Googlo Shoots"`.|
|rowsChanged|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of rows changed.|
|sheetsChanged|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of sheets changed.|
|valuesChanged|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of non-formula cells changed.|

Data in the grid, as well as metadata about the dimensions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|columnMetadata|[[DimensionProperties](#schemadimensionproperties)]|false|none|Metadata about the requested columns in the grid, starting with the column in start_column.|
|rowData|[[RowData](#schemarowdata)]|false|none|The data in the grid, one entry per row, starting with the row in startRow. The values in RowData will correspond to columns starting at start_column.|
|rowMetadata|[[DimensionProperties](#schemadimensionproperties)]|false|none|Metadata about the requested rows in the grid, starting with the row in start_row.|
|startColumn|integer(int32)|false|none|The first column this GridData refers to, zero-based.|
|startRow|integer(int32)|false|none|The first row this GridData refers to, zero-based.|

<h2 id="tocS_GridRange">GridRange</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemagridrange"></a>
<a id="schema_GridRange"></a>
<a id="tocSgridrange"></a>
<a id="tocsgridrange"></a>

```json
{
  "endColumnIndex": 0,
  "endRowIndex": 0,
  "sheetId": 0,
  "startColumnIndex": 0,
  "startRowIndex": 0
}
```

A range on a sheet. All indexes are zero-based. Indexes are half open, i.e. the start index is inclusive and the end index is exclusive -- [start_index, end_index). Missing indexes indicate the range is unbounded on that side. For example, if `"Sheet1"` is sheet ID 123456, then: `Sheet1!A1:A1 == sheet_id: 123456, start_row_index: 0, end_row_index: 1, start_column_index: 0, end_column_index: 1` `Sheet1!A3:B4 == sheet_id: 123456, start_row_index: 2, end_row_index: 4, start_column_index: 0, end_column_index: 2` `Sheet1!A:B == sheet_id: 123456, start_column_index: 0, end_column_index: 2` `Sheet1!A5:B == sheet_id: 123456, start_row_index: 4, start_column_index: 0, end_column_index: 2` `Sheet1 == sheet_id: 123456` The start index must always be less than or equal to the end index. If the start index equals the end index, then the range is empty. Empty ranges are typically not meaningful and are usually rendered in the UI as `#REF!`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|endColumnIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The end column (exclusive) of the range, or not set if unbounded.|
|endRowIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The end row (exclusive) of the range, or not set if unbounded.|
|sheetId|integer(int32)|false|none|The sheet this range is on.|
|startColumnIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The start column (inclusive) of the range, or not set if unbounded.|
|startRowIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The start row (inclusive) of the range, or not set if unbounded.|
