
A histogram chart. A histogram chart groups data items into bins, displaying each bin as a column of stacked items. Histograms are used to display the distribution of a dataset. Each column of items represents a range into which those items fall. The number of bins can be chosen automatically or specified explicitly.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bucketSize|number(double)|false|none|By default the bucket size (the range of values stacked in a single column) is chosen automatically, but it may be overridden here. E.g., A bucket size of 1.5 results in buckets from 0 - 1.5, 1.5 - 3.0, etc. Cannot be negative. This field is optional.|
|legendPosition|string|false|none|The position of the chart legend.|
|outlierPercentile|number(double)|false|none|The outlier percentile is used to ensure that outliers do not adversely affect the calculation of bucket sizes. For example, setting an outlier percentile of 0.05 indicates that the top and bottom 5% of values when calculating buckets. The values are still included in the chart, they will be added to the first or last buckets instead of their own buckets. Must be between 0.0 and 0.5.|
|series|[[HistogramSeries](#schemahistogramseries)]|false|none|The series for a histogram may be either a single series of values to be bucketed or multiple series, each of the same length, containing the name of the series followed by the values to be bucketed for that series.|
|showItemDividers|boolean|false|none|Whether horizontal divider lines should be displayed between items in each column.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|legendPosition|HISTOGRAM_CHART_LEGEND_POSITION_UNSPECIFIED|
|legendPosition|BOTTOM_LEGEND|
|legendPosition|LEFT_LEGEND|
|legendPosition|RIGHT_LEGEND|
|legendPosition|TOP_LEGEND|
|legendPosition|NO_LEGEND|
|legendPosition|INSIDE_LEGEND|

<h2 id="tocS_HistogramRule">HistogramRule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahistogramrule"></a>
<a id="schema_HistogramRule"></a>
<a id="tocShistogramrule"></a>
<a id="tocshistogramrule"></a>

```json
{
  "end": 0,
  "interval": 0,
  "start": 0
}
```

Allows you to organize the numeric values in a source data column into buckets of a constant size. All values from HistogramRule.start to HistogramRule.end are placed into groups of size HistogramRule.interval. In addition, all values below HistogramRule.start are placed in one group, and all values above HistogramRule.end are placed in another. Only HistogramRule.interval is required, though if HistogramRule.start and HistogramRule.end are both provided, HistogramRule.start must be less than HistogramRule.end. For example, a pivot table showing average purchase amount by age that has 50+ rows: +-----+-------------------+ | Age | AVERAGE of Amount | +-----+-------------------+ | 16 | $27.13 | | 17 | $5.24 | | 18 | $20.15 | ... +-----+-------------------+ could be turned into a pivot table that looks like the one below by applying a histogram group rule with a HistogramRule.start of 25, an HistogramRule.interval of 20, and an HistogramRule.end of 65. +-------------+-------------------+ | Grouped Age | AVERAGE of Amount | +-------------+-------------------+ | < 25 | $19.34 | | 25-45 | $31.43 | | 45-65 | $35.87 | | > 65 | $27.55 | +-------------+-------------------+ | Grand Total | $29.12 | +-------------+-------------------+

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|end|number(double)|false|none|The maximum value at which items are placed into buckets of constant size. Values above end are lumped into a single bucket. This field is optional.|
|interval|number(double)|false|none|The size of the buckets that are created. Must be positive.|
|start|number(double)|false|none|The minimum value at which items are placed into buckets of constant size. Values below start are lumped into a single bucket. This field is optional.|

```json
  }
}
```

Inserts rows or columns in a sheet at a particular index.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inheritFromBefore|boolean|false|none|Whether dimension properties should be extended from the dimensions before or after the newly inserted dimensions. True to inherit from the dimensions before (in which case the start index must be greater than 0), and false to inherit from the dimensions after. For example, if row index 0 has red background and row index 1 has a green background, then inserting 2 rows at index 1 can inherit either the green or red background. If `inheritFromBefore` is true, the two new rows will be red (because the row before the insertion point was red), whereas if `inheritFromBefore` is false, the two new rows will be green (because the row after the insertion point was green).|
|range|[DimensionRange](#schemadimensionrange)|false|none|The dimensions to insert. Both the start and end indexes must be bounded.|

<h2 id="tocS_Interval">Interval</h2>

```json
{
  "endTime": "string",
  "startTime": "string"
}
```

Represents a time interval, encoded as a Timestamp start (inclusive) and a Timestamp end (exclusive). The start must be less than or equal to the end. When the start equals the end, the interval is empty (matches no time). When both start and end are unspecified, the interval matches any time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|endTime|string(google-datetime)|false|none|Optional. Exclusive end of the interval. If specified, a Timestamp matching this interval will have to be before the end.|
|startTime|string(google-datetime)|false|none|Optional. Inclusive start of the interval. If specified, a Timestamp matching this interval will have to be the same or after the start.|

<h2 id="tocS_ManualRule">ManualRule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamanualrule"></a>
<a id="schema_ManualRule"></a>
<a id="tocSmanualrule"></a>

```json
{
  "groups": [
    {
      "groupName": {
        "boolValue": true,
        "errorValue": {
          "message": "string",
          "type": "ERROR_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
        },
        "formulaValue": "string",
        "numberValue": 0,
        "stringValue": "string"
      },
      "items": [
        {
          "boolValue": true,
          "errorValue": {
            "message": "string",
            "type": "ERROR_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
          },
          "formulaValue": "string",
          "numberValue": 0,
          "stringValue": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Allows you to manually organize the values in a source data column into buckets with names of your choosing. For example, a pivot table that aggregates population by state: +-------+-------------------+ | State | SUM of Population | +-------+-------------------+ | AK | 0.7 | | AL | 4.8 | | AR | 2.9 | ... +-------+-------------------+ could be turned into a pivot table that aggregates population by time zone by providing a list of groups (for example, groupName = 'Central', items = ['AL', 'AR', 'IA', ...]) to a manual group rule. Note that a similar effect could be achieved by adding a time zone column to the source data and adjusting the pivot table. +-----------+-------------------+ | Time Zone | SUM of Population | +-----------+-------------------+ | Central | 106.3 | | Eastern | 151.9 | | Mountain | 17.4 | ... +-----------+-------------------+

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groups|[[ManualRuleGroup](#schemamanualrulegroup)]|false|none|The list of group names and the corresponding items from the source data that map to each group name.|


An org chart. Org charts require a unique set of labels in labels and may optionally include parent_labels and tooltips. parent_labels contain, for each node, the label identifying the parent node. tooltips contain, for each node, an optional tooltip. For example, to describe an OrgChart with Alice as the CEO, Bob as the President (reporting to Alice) and Cathy as VP of Sales (also reporting to Alice), have labels contain "Alice", "Bob", "Cathy", parent_labels contain "", "Alice", "Alice" and tooltips contain "CEO", "President", "VP Sales".

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|labels|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data containing the labels for all the nodes in the chart. Labels must be unique.|
|nodeColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The color of the org chart nodes. Deprecated: Use node_color_style.|
|nodeColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The color of the org chart nodes. If node_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|
|nodeSize|string|false|none|The size of the org chart nodes.|
|parentLabels|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data containing the label of the parent for the corresponding node. A blank value indicates that the node has no parent and is a top-level node. This field is optional.|
|selectedNodeColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The color of the selected org chart nodes. Deprecated: Use selected_node_color_style.|
|selectedNodeColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The color of the selected org chart nodes. If selected_node_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|
|tooltips|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data containing the tooltip for the corresponding node. A blank value results in no tooltip being displayed for the node. This field is optional.|

#### Enumerated Values

<h2 id="tocS_PivotFilterCriteria">PivotFilterCriteria</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapivotfiltercriteria"></a>
<a id="schema_PivotFilterCriteria"></a>
<a id="tocSpivotfiltercriteria"></a>
<a id="tocspivotfiltercriteria"></a>

```json
{
  "condition": {
    "type": "CONDITION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
    "values": [
      {
        "relativeDate": "RELATIVE_DATE_UNSPECIFIED",
        "userEnteredValue": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "visibleByDefault": true,
  "visibleValues": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

Criteria for showing/hiding rows in a pivot table.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|condition|[BooleanCondition](#schemabooleancondition)|false|none|A condition that must be true for values to be shown. (`visibleValues` does not override this -- even if a value is listed there, it is still hidden if it does not meet the condition.) Condition values that refer to ranges in A1-notation are evaluated relative to the pivot table sheet. References are treated absolutely, so are not filled down the pivot table. For example, a condition value of `=A1` on "Pivot Table 1" is treated as `'Pivot Table 1'!$A$1`. The source data of the pivot table can be referenced by column header name. For example, if the source data has columns named "Revenue" and "Cost" and a condition is applied to the "Revenue" column with type `NUMBER_GREATER` and value `=Cost`, then only columns where "Revenue" > "Cost" are included.|
|visibleByDefault|boolean|false|none|Whether values are visible by default. If true, the visible_values are ignored, all values that meet condition (if specified) are shown. If false, values that are both in visible_values and meet condition are shown.|
|visibleValues|[string]|false|none|Values that should be included. Values not listed here are excluded.|

```json
      }
```


A single grouping (either row or column) in a pivot table.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dataSourceColumnReference|[DataSourceColumnReference](#schemadatasourcecolumnreference)|false|none|The reference to the data source column this grouping is based on.|
|groupLimit|[PivotGroupLimit](#schemapivotgrouplimit)|false|none|The count limit on rows or columns to apply to this pivot group.|
|groupRule|[PivotGroupRule](#schemapivotgrouprule)|false|none|The group rule to apply to this row/column group.|
|label|string|false|none|The labels to use for the row/column groups which can be customized. For example, in the following pivot table, the row label is `Region` (which could be renamed to `State`) and the column label is `Product` (which could be renamed `Item`). Pivot tables created before December 2017 do not have header labels. If you'd like to add header labels to an existing pivot table, please delete the existing pivot table and then create a new pivot table with same parameters. +--------------+---------+-------+ \| SUM of Units \| Product \| \| \| Region \| Pen \| Paper \| +--------------+---------+-------+ \| New York \| 345 \| 98 \| \| Oregon \| 234 \| 123 \| \| Tennessee \| 531 \| 415 \| +--------------+---------+-------+ \| Grand Total \| 1110 \| 636 \| +--------------+---------+-------+|
|repeatHeadings|boolean|false|none|True if the headings in this pivot group should be repeated. This is only valid for row groupings and is ignored by columns. By default, we minimize repetition of headings by not showing higher level headings where they are the same. For example, even though the third row below corresponds to "Q1 Mar", "Q1" is not shown because it is redundant with previous rows. Setting repeat_headings to true would cause "Q1" to be repeated for "Feb" and "Mar". +--------------+ \| Q1 \| Jan \| \| \| Feb \| \| \| Mar \| +--------+-----+ \| Q1 Total \| +--------------+|
|showTotals|boolean|false|none|True if the pivot table should include the totals for this grouping.|
|sortOrder|string|false|none|The order the values in this group should be sorted.|
|sourceColumnOffset|integer(int32)|false|none|The column offset of the source range that this grouping is based on. For example, if the source was `C10:E15`, a `sourceColumnOffset` of `0` means this group refers to column `C`, whereas the offset `1` would refer to column `D`.|
|valueBucket|[PivotGroupSortValueBucket](#schemapivotgroupsortvaluebucket)|false|none|The bucket of the opposite pivot group to sort by. If not specified, sorting is alphabetical by this group's values.|
|valueMetadata|[[PivotGroupValueMetadata](#schemapivotgroupvaluemetadata)]|false|none|Metadata about values in the grouping.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|sortOrder|SORT_ORDER_UNSPECIFIED|
|sortOrder|ASCENDING|
|sortOrder|DESCENDING|

Information about which values in a pivot group should be used for sorting.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buckets|[[ExtendedValue](#schemaextendedvalue)]|false|none|Determines the bucket from which values are chosen to sort. For example, in a pivot table with one row group & two column groups, the row group can list up to two values. The first value corresponds to a value within the first column group, and the second value corresponds to a value in the second column group. If no values are listed, this would indicate that the row should be sorted according to the "Grand Total" over the column groups. If a single value is listed, this would correspond to using the "Total" of that bucket.|
|valuesIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The offset in the PivotTable.values list which the values in this grouping should be sorted by.|

|criteria|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** An optional mapping of filters per source column offset. The filters are applied before aggregating data into the pivot table. The map's key is the column offset of the source range that you want to filter, and the value is the criteria for that column. For example, if the source was `C10:E15`, a key of `0` will have the filter for column `C`, whereas the key `1` is for column `D`. This field is deprecated in favor of filter_specs.|
|dataExecutionStatus|[DataExecutionStatus](#schemadataexecutionstatus)|false|none|Output only. The data execution status for data source pivot tables.|
|dataSourceId|string|false|none|The ID of the data source the pivot table is reading data from.|
|filterSpecs|[[PivotFilterSpec](#schemapivotfilterspec)]|false|none|The filters applied to the source columns before aggregating data for the pivot table. Both criteria and filter_specs are populated in responses. If both fields are specified in an update request, this field takes precedence.|
|rows|[[PivotGroup](#schemapivotgroup)]|false|none|Each row grouping in the pivot table.|
|source|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range the pivot table is reading data from.|
|valueLayout|string|false|none|Whether values should be listed horizontally (as columns) or vertically (as rows).|
|values|[[PivotValue](#schemapivotvalue)]|false|none|A list of values to include in the pivot table.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|valueLayout|HORIZONTAL|
|valueLayout|VERTICAL|

<h2 id="tocS_PivotValue">PivotValue</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapivotvalue"></a>
<a id="schema_PivotValue"></a>
<a id="tocSpivotvalue"></a>
<a id="tocspivotvalue"></a>

```json
{
  "calculatedDisplayType": "PIVOT_VALUE_CALCULATED_DISPLAY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "dataSourceColumnReference": {
    "name": "string"
  },
  "formula": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "sourceColumnOffset": 0,
  "summarizeFunction": "PIVOT_STANDARD_VALUE_FUNCTION_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

The definition of how a value in a pivot table should be calculated.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|calculatedDisplayType|string|false|none|If specified, indicates that pivot values should be displayed as the result of a calculation with another pivot value. For example, if calculated_display_type is specified as PERCENT_OF_GRAND_TOTAL, all the pivot values are displayed as the percentage of the grand total. In the Sheets editor, this is referred to as "Show As" in the value section of a pivot table.|
|dataSourceColumnReference|[DataSourceColumnReference](#schemadatasourcecolumnreference)|false|none|The reference to the data source column that this value reads from.|
|formula|string|false|none|A custom formula to calculate the value. The formula must start with an `=` character.|
|name|string|false|none|A name to use for the value.|
|sourceColumnOffset|integer(int32)|false|none|The column offset of the source range that this value reads from. For example, if the source was `C10:E15`, a `sourceColumnOffset` of `0` means this value refers to column `C`, whereas the offset `1` would refer to column `D`.|
|summarizeFunction|string|false|none|A function to summarize the value. If formula is set, the only supported values are SUM and CUSTOM. If sourceColumnOffset is set, then `CUSTOM` is not supported.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|calculatedDisplayType|PIVOT_VALUE_CALCULATED_DISPLAY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|calculatedDisplayType|PERCENT_OF_ROW_TOTAL|
|calculatedDisplayType|PERCENT_OF_COLUMN_TOTAL|
|calculatedDisplayType|PERCENT_OF_GRAND_TOTAL|
|summarizeFunction|PIVOT_STANDARD_VALUE_FUNCTION_UNSPECIFIED|
|summarizeFunction|SUM|
|summarizeFunction|COUNTA|
|summarizeFunction|COUNT|
|summarizeFunction|COUNTUNIQUE|
|summarizeFunction|AVERAGE|
|summarizeFunction|MAX|
|summarizeFunction|MIN|
|summarizeFunction|MEDIAN|
|summarizeFunction|PRODUCT|
|summarizeFunction|STDEV|
|summarizeFunction|STDEVP|
|summarizeFunction|VAR|
|summarizeFunction|VARP|
|summarizeFunction|CUSTOM|

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "editors": {
    "domainUsersCanEdit": true,
    "groups": [
      "string"
    ],
    "users": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "namedRangeId": "string",
  "protectedRangeId": 0,
  "range": {
    "endColumnIndex": 0,
    "endRowIndex": 0,
    "sheetId": 0,
    "startColumnIndex": 0,
    "startRowIndex": 0
  },
  "requestingUserCanEdit": true,
  "unprotectedRanges": [
    {
      "endColumnIndex": 0,
      "endRowIndex": 0,
      "sheetId": 0,
      "startColumnIndex": 0,
      "startRowIndex": 0
    }
  ],
  "warningOnly": true
}
```

A protected range.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|The description of this protected range.|
|editors|[Editors](#schemaeditors)|false|none|The users and groups with edit access to the protected range. This field is only visible to users with edit access to the protected range and the document. Editors are not supported with warning_only protection.|
|namedRangeId|string|false|none|The named range this protected range is backed by, if any. When writing, only one of range or named_range_id may be set.|
|protectedRangeId|integer(int32)|false|none|The ID of the protected range. This field is read-only.|
|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range that is being protected. The range may be fully unbounded, in which case this is considered a protected sheet. When writing, only one of range or named_range_id may be set.|
|requestingUserCanEdit|boolean|false|none|True if the user who requested this protected range can edit the protected area. This field is read-only.|
|unprotectedRanges|[[GridRange](#schemagridrange)]|false|none|The list of unprotected ranges within a protected sheet. Unprotected ranges are only supported on protected sheets.|
|warningOnly|boolean|false|none|True if this protected range will show a warning when editing. Warning-based protection means that every user can edit data in the protected range, except editing will prompt a warning asking the user to confirm the edit. When writing: if this field is true, then editors are ignored. Additionally, if this field is changed from true to false and the `editors` field is not set (nor included in the field mask), then the editors will be set to all the editors in the document.|

<h2 id="tocS_RefreshDataSourceRequest">RefreshDataSourceRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarefreshdatasourcerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_RefreshDataSourceRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSrefreshdatasourcerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsrefreshdatasourcerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "dataSourceId": "string",
  "force": true,
  "isAll": true,
  "references": {
    "references": [
      {
        "chartId": 0,
        "dataSourceFormulaCell": {
          "columnIndex": 0,
          "rowIndex": 0,
          "sheetId": 0
        },
        "dataSourcePivotTableAnchorCell": {
          "columnIndex": 0,
          "rowIndex": 0,
          "sheetId": 0
        },
        "dataSourceTableAnchorCell": {
          "columnIndex": 0,
          "rowIndex": 0,
          "sheetId": 0
        },
        "sheetId": "string"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Refreshes one or multiple data source objects in the spreadsheet by the specified references. The request requires an additional `bigquery.readonly` OAuth scope. If there are multiple refresh requests referencing the same data source objects in one batch, only the last refresh request is processed, and all those requests will have the same response accordingly.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dataSourceId|string|false|none|Reference to a DataSource. If specified, refreshes all associated data source objects for the data source.|
|force|boolean|false|none|Refreshes the data source objects regardless of the current state. If not set and a referenced data source object was in error state, the refresh will fail immediately.|
|isAll|boolean|false|none|Refreshes all existing data source objects in the spreadsheet.|
|references|[DataSourceObjectReferences](#schemadatasourceobjectreferences)|false|none|References to data source objects to refresh.|


Updates all cells in the range to the values in the given Cell object. Only the fields listed in the fields field are updated; others are unchanged. If writing a cell with a formula, the formula's ranges will automatically increment for each field in the range. For example, if writing a cell with formula `=A1` into range B2:C4, B2 would be `=A1`, B3 would be `=A2`, B4 would be `=A3`, C2 would be `=B1`, C3 would be `=B2`, C4 would be `=B3`. To keep the formula's ranges static, use the `$` indicator. For example, use the formula `=$A$1` to prevent both the row and the column from incrementing.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cell|[CellData](#schemacelldata)|false|none|The data to write.|
|fields|string(google-fieldmask)|false|none|The fields that should be updated. At least one field must be specified. The root `cell` is implied and should not be specified. A single `"*"` can be used as short-hand for listing every field.|
|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range to repeat the cell in.|

A single kind of update to apply to a spreadsheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|addBanding|[AddBandingRequest](#schemaaddbandingrequest)|false|none|Adds a new banded range|
|addChart|[AddChartRequest](#schemaaddchartrequest)|false|none|Adds a chart.|
|addConditionalFormatRule|[AddConditionalFormatRuleRequest](#schemaaddconditionalformatrulerequest)|false|none|Adds a new conditional format rule.|
|addDataSource|[AddDataSourceRequest](#schemaadddatasourcerequest)|false|none|Adds a data source.|
|addDimensionGroup|[AddDimensionGroupRequest](#schemaadddimensiongrouprequest)|false|none|Creates a group over the specified range.|
|addFilterView|[AddFilterViewRequest](#schemaaddfilterviewrequest)|false|none|Adds a filter view.|
|addNamedRange|[AddNamedRangeRequest](#schemaaddnamedrangerequest)|false|none|Adds a named range.|
|addProtectedRange|[AddProtectedRangeRequest](#schemaaddprotectedrangerequest)|false|none|Adds a protected range.|
|addSheet|[AddSheetRequest](#schemaaddsheetrequest)|false|none|Adds a sheet.|
|addSlicer|[AddSlicerRequest](#schemaaddslicerrequest)|false|none|Adds a slicer.|
|appendCells|[AppendCellsRequest](#schemaappendcellsrequest)|false|none|Appends cells after the last row with data in a sheet.|
|appendDimension|[AppendDimensionRequest](#schemaappenddimensionrequest)|false|none|Appends dimensions to the end of a sheet.|
|autoFill|[AutoFillRequest](#schemaautofillrequest)|false|none|Automatically fills in more data based on existing data.|
|autoResizeDimensions|[AutoResizeDimensionsRequest](#schemaautoresizedimensionsrequest)|false|none|Automatically resizes one or more dimensions based on the contents of the cells in that dimension.|
|clearBasicFilter|[ClearBasicFilterRequest](#schemaclearbasicfilterrequest)|false|none|Clears the basic filter on a sheet.|
|copyPaste|[CopyPasteRequest](#schemacopypasterequest)|false|none|Copies data from one area and pastes it to another.|
|createDeveloperMetadata|[CreateDeveloperMetadataRequest](#schemacreatedevelopermetadatarequest)|false|none|Creates new developer metadata|
|cutPaste|[CutPasteRequest](#schemacutpasterequest)|false|none|Cuts data from one area and pastes it to another.|
|deleteBanding|[DeleteBandingRequest](#schemadeletebandingrequest)|false|none|Removes a banded range|
|deleteConditionalFormatRule|[DeleteConditionalFormatRuleRequest](#schemadeleteconditionalformatrulerequest)|false|none|Deletes an existing conditional format rule.|
|deleteDataSource|[DeleteDataSourceRequest](#schemadeletedatasourcerequest)|false|none|Deletes a data source.|
|deleteDeveloperMetadata|[DeleteDeveloperMetadataRequest](#schemadeletedevelopermetadatarequest)|false|none|Deletes developer metadata|
|deleteDimension|[DeleteDimensionRequest](#schemadeletedimensionrequest)|false|none|Deletes rows or columns in a sheet.|
|deleteDimensionGroup|[DeleteDimensionGroupRequest](#schemadeletedimensiongrouprequest)|false|none|Deletes a group over the specified range.|
|deleteDuplicates|[DeleteDuplicatesRequest](#schemadeleteduplicatesrequest)|false|none|Removes rows containing duplicate values in specified columns of a cell range.|
|deleteEmbeddedObject|[DeleteEmbeddedObjectRequest](#schemadeleteembeddedobjectrequest)|false|none|Deletes an embedded object (e.g, chart, image) in a sheet.|
|deleteFilterView|[DeleteFilterViewRequest](#schemadeletefilterviewrequest)|false|none|Deletes a filter view from a sheet.|
|deleteNamedRange|[DeleteNamedRangeRequest](#schemadeletenamedrangerequest)|false|none|Deletes a named range.|
|deleteProtectedRange|[DeleteProtectedRangeRequest](#schemadeleteprotectedrangerequest)|false|none|Deletes a protected range.|
|deleteRange|[DeleteRangeRequest](#schemadeleterangerequest)|false|none|Deletes a range of cells from a sheet, shifting the remaining cells.|
|deleteSheet|[DeleteSheetRequest](#schemadeletesheetrequest)|false|none|Deletes a sheet.|
|duplicateFilterView|[DuplicateFilterViewRequest](#schemaduplicatefilterviewrequest)|false|none|Duplicates a filter view.|
|duplicateSheet|[DuplicateSheetRequest](#schemaduplicatesheetrequest)|false|none|Duplicates a sheet.|
|findReplace|[FindReplaceRequest](#schemafindreplacerequest)|false|none|Finds and replaces occurrences of some text with other text.|
|insertDimension|[InsertDimensionRequest](#schemainsertdimensionrequest)|false|none|Inserts new rows or columns in a sheet.|
|insertRange|[InsertRangeRequest](#schemainsertrangerequest)|false|none|Inserts new cells in a sheet, shifting the existing cells.|
|mergeCells|[MergeCellsRequest](#schemamergecellsrequest)|false|none|Merges cells together.|
|moveDimension|[MoveDimensionRequest](#schemamovedimensionrequest)|false|none|Moves rows or columns to another location in a sheet.|
|pasteData|[PasteDataRequest](#schemapastedatarequest)|false|none|Pastes data (HTML or delimited) into a sheet.|
|randomizeRange|[RandomizeRangeRequest](#schemarandomizerangerequest)|false|none|Randomizes the order of the rows in a range.|
|refreshDataSource|[RefreshDataSourceRequest](#schemarefreshdatasourcerequest)|false|none|Refreshes one or multiple data sources and associated dbobjects.|
|repeatCell|[RepeatCellRequest](#schemarepeatcellrequest)|false|none|Repeats a single cell across a range.|
|setBasicFilter|[SetBasicFilterRequest](#schemasetbasicfilterrequest)|false|none|Sets the basic filter on a sheet.|
|setDataValidation|[SetDataValidationRequest](#schemasetdatavalidationrequest)|false|none|Sets data validation for one or more cells.|
|sortRange|[SortRangeRequest](#schemasortrangerequest)|false|none|Sorts data in a range.|
|textToColumns|[TextToColumnsRequest](#schematexttocolumnsrequest)|false|none|Converts a column of text into many columns of text.|
|trimWhitespace|[TrimWhitespaceRequest](#schematrimwhitespacerequest)|false|none|Trims cells of whitespace (such as spaces, tabs, or new lines).|
|unmergeCells|[UnmergeCellsRequest](#schemaunmergecellsrequest)|false|none|Unmerges merged cells.|
|updateBanding|[UpdateBandingRequest](#schemaupdatebandingrequest)|false|none|Updates a banded range|
|updateBorders|[UpdateBordersRequest](#schemaupdatebordersrequest)|false|none|Updates the borders in a range of cells.|
|updateCells|[UpdateCellsRequest](#schemaupdatecellsrequest)|false|none|Updates many cells at once.|
|updateChartSpec|[UpdateChartSpecRequest](#schemaupdatechartspecrequest)|false|none|Updates a chart's specifications.|
|updateConditionalFormatRule|[UpdateConditionalFormatRuleRequest](#schemaupdateconditionalformatrulerequest)|false|none|Updates an existing conditional format rule.|
|updateDataSource|[UpdateDataSourceRequest](#schemaupdatedatasourcerequest)|false|none|Updates a data source.|
|updateDeveloperMetadata|[UpdateDeveloperMetadataRequest](#schemaupdatedevelopermetadatarequest)|false|none|Updates an existing developer metadata entry|
|updateDimensionGroup|[UpdateDimensionGroupRequest](#schemaupdatedimensiongrouprequest)|false|none|Updates the state of the specified group.|
|updateDimensionProperties|[UpdateDimensionPropertiesRequest](#schemaupdatedimensionpropertiesrequest)|false|none|Updates dimensions' properties.|
|updateEmbeddedObjectBorder|[UpdateEmbeddedObjectBorderRequest](#schemaupdateembeddedobjectborderrequest)|false|none|Updates an embedded object's border.|
|updateEmbeddedObjectPosition|[UpdateEmbeddedObjectPositionRequest](#schemaupdateembeddedobjectpositionrequest)|false|none|Updates an embedded object's (e.g. chart, image) position.|
|updateFilterView|[UpdateFilterViewRequest](#schemaupdatefilterviewrequest)|false|none|Updates the properties of a filter view.|
|updateNamedRange|[UpdateNamedRangeRequest](#schemaupdatenamedrangerequest)|false|none|Updates a named range.|
|updateProtectedRange|[UpdateProtectedRangeRequest](#schemaupdateprotectedrangerequest)|false|none|Updates a protected range.|
|updateSheetProperties|[UpdateSheetPropertiesRequest](#schemaupdatesheetpropertiesrequest)|false|none|Updates a sheet's properties.|
|updateSlicerSpec|[UpdateSlicerSpecRequest](#schemaupdateslicerspecrequest)|false|none|Updates a slicer's specifications.|
|updateSpreadsheetProperties|[UpdateSpreadsheetPropertiesRequest](#schemaupdatespreadsheetpropertiesrequest)|false|none|Updates the spreadsheet's properties.|

A scorecard chart. Scorecard charts are used to highlight key performance indicators, known as KPIs, on the spreadsheet. A scorecard chart can represent things like total sales, average cost, or a top selling item. You can specify a single data value, or aggregate over a range of data. Percentage or absolute difference from a baseline value can be highlighted, like changes over time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregateType|string|false|none|The aggregation type for key and baseline chart data in scorecard chart. This field is not supported for data source charts. Use the ChartData.aggregateType field of the key_value_data or baseline_value_data instead for data source charts. This field is optional.|
|baselineValueData|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data for scorecard baseline value. This field is optional.|
|baselineValueFormat|[BaselineValueFormat](#schemabaselinevalueformat)|false|none|Formatting options for baseline value. This field is needed only if baseline_value_data is specified.|
|customFormatOptions|[ChartCustomNumberFormatOptions](#schemachartcustomnumberformatoptions)|false|none|Custom formatting options for numeric key/baseline values in scorecard chart. This field is used only when number_format_source is set to CUSTOM. This field is optional.|
|keyValueData|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data for scorecard key value.|
|keyValueFormat|[KeyValueFormat](#schemakeyvalueformat)|false|none|Formatting options for key value.|
|numberFormatSource|string|false|none|The number format source used in the scorecard chart. This field is optional.|
|scaleFactor|number(double)|false|none|Value to scale scorecard key and baseline value. For example, a factor of 10 can be used to divide all values in the chart by 10. This field is optional.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregateType|CHART_AGGREGATE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|aggregateType|AVERAGE|
|aggregateType|COUNT|
|aggregateType|MAX|
|aggregateType|MEDIAN|
|aggregateType|MIN|
|aggregateType|SUM|
|numberFormatSource|CHART_NUMBER_FORMAT_SOURCE_UNDEFINED|
|numberFormatSource|FROM_DATA|
|numberFormatSource|CUSTOM|

A sheet in a spreadsheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bandedRanges|[[BandedRange](#schemabandedrange)]|false|none|The banded (alternating colors) ranges on this sheet.|
|basicFilter|[BasicFilter](#schemabasicfilter)|false|none|The filter on this sheet, if any.|
|charts|[[EmbeddedChart](#schemaembeddedchart)]|false|none|The specifications of every chart on this sheet.|
|columnGroups|[[DimensionGroup](#schemadimensiongroup)]|false|none|All column groups on this sheet, ordered by increasing range start index, then by group depth.|
|conditionalFormats|[[ConditionalFormatRule](#schemaconditionalformatrule)]|false|none|The conditional format rules in this sheet.|
|data|[[GridData](#schemagriddata)]|false|none|Data in the grid, if this is a grid sheet. The number of GridData objects returned is dependent on the number of ranges requested on this sheet. For example, if this is representing `Sheet1`, and the spreadsheet was requested with ranges `Sheet1!A1:C10` and `Sheet1!D15:E20`, then the first GridData will have a startRow/startColumn of `0`, while the second one will have `startRow 14` (zero-based row 15), and `startColumn 3` (zero-based column D). For a DATA_SOURCE sheet, you can not request a specific range, the GridData contains all the values.|
|developerMetadata|[[DeveloperMetadata](#schemadevelopermetadata)]|false|none|The developer metadata associated with a sheet.|
|filterViews|[[FilterView](#schemafilterview)]|false|none|The filter views in this sheet.|
|merges|[[GridRange](#schemagridrange)]|false|none|The ranges that are merged together.|
|properties|[SheetProperties](#schemasheetproperties)|false|none|The properties of the sheet.|
|protectedRanges|[[ProtectedRange](#schemaprotectedrange)]|false|none|The protected ranges in this sheet.|
|rowGroups|[[DimensionGroup](#schemadimensiongroup)]|false|none|All row groups on this sheet, ordered by increasing range start index, then by group depth.|
|slicers|[[Slicer](#schemaslicer)]|false|none|The slicers on this sheet.|

Properties of a sheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dataSourceSheetProperties|[DataSourceSheetProperties](#schemadatasourcesheetproperties)|false|none|Output only. If present, the field contains DATA_SOURCE sheet specific properties.|
|gridProperties|[GridProperties](#schemagridproperties)|false|none|Additional properties of the sheet if this sheet is a grid. (If the sheet is an object sheet, containing a chart or image, then this field will be absent.) When writing it is an error to set any grid properties on non-grid sheets. If this sheet is a DATA_SOURCE sheet, this field is output only but contains the properties that reflect how a data source sheet is rendered in the UI, e.g. row_count.|
|hidden|boolean|false|none|True if the sheet is hidden in the UI, false if it's visible.|
|index|integer(int32)|false|none|The index of the sheet within the spreadsheet. When adding or updating sheet properties, if this field is excluded then the sheet is added or moved to the end of the sheet list. When updating sheet indices or inserting sheets, movement is considered in "before the move" indexes. For example, if there were three sheets (S1, S2, S3) in order to move S1 ahead of S2 the index would have to be set to 2. A sheet index update request is ignored if the requested index is identical to the sheets current index or if the requested new index is equal to the current sheet index + 1.|
|rightToLeft|boolean|false|none|True if the sheet is an RTL sheet instead of an LTR sheet.|
|sheetId|integer(int32)|false|none|The ID of the sheet. Must be non-negative. This field cannot be changed once set.|
|sheetType|string|false|none|The type of sheet. Defaults to GRID. This field cannot be changed once set.|
|tabColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The color of the tab in the UI. Deprecated: Use tab_color_style.|
|tabColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The color of the tab in the UI. If tab_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|
|title|string|false|none|The name of the sheet.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|sheetType|SHEET_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|sheetType|GRID|
|sheetType|OBJECT|
|sheetType|DATA_SOURCE|

|foregroundColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The foreground color to sort by; cells with this foreground color are sorted to the top. Mutually exclusive with background_color, and must be an RGB-type color. If foreground_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|

Resource that represents a spreadsheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dataSourceSchedules|[[DataSourceRefreshSchedule](#schemadatasourcerefreshschedule)]|false|read-only|Output only. A list of data source refresh schedules.|
|dataSources|[[DataSource](#schemadatasource)]|false|none|A list of external data sources connected with the spreadsheet.|
|developerMetadata|[[DeveloperMetadata](#schemadevelopermetadata)]|false|none|The developer metadata associated with a spreadsheet.|
|namedRanges|[[NamedRange](#schemanamedrange)]|false|none|The named ranges defined in a spreadsheet.|
|properties|[SpreadsheetProperties](#schemaspreadsheetproperties)|false|none|Overall properties of a spreadsheet.|
|sheets|[[Sheet](#schemasheet)]|false|none|The sheets that are part of a spreadsheet.|
|spreadsheetId|string|false|none|The ID of the spreadsheet. This field is read-only.|
|spreadsheetUrl|string|false|none|The url of the spreadsheet. This field is read-only.|

Properties of a spreadsheet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|autoRecalc|string|false|none|The amount of time to wait before volatile functions are recalculated.|
|defaultFormat|[CellFormat](#schemacellformat)|false|none|The default format of all cells in the spreadsheet. CellData.effectiveFormat will not be set if the cell's format is equal to this default format. This field is read-only.|
|iterativeCalculationSettings|[IterativeCalculationSettings](#schemaiterativecalculationsettings)|false|none|Determines whether and how circular references are resolved with iterative calculation. Absence of this field means that circular references result in calculation errors.|
|locale|string|false|none|The locale of the spreadsheet in one of the following formats: * an ISO 639-1 language code such as `en` * an ISO 639-2 language code such as `fil`, if no 639-1 code exists * a combination of the ISO language code and country code, such as `en_US` Note: when updating this field, not all locales/languages are supported.|
|spreadsheetTheme|[SpreadsheetTheme](#schemaspreadsheettheme)|false|none|Theme applied to the spreadsheet.|
|timeZone|string|false|none|The time zone of the spreadsheet, in CLDR format such as `America/New_York`. If the time zone isn't recognized, this may be a custom time zone such as `GMT-07:00`.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the spreadsheet.|

```json
  "minutes": 0,
  "nanos": 0,
  "seconds": 0
}
```

Represents a time of day. The date and time zone are either not significant or are specified elsewhere. An API may choose to allow leap seconds. Related types are google.type.Date and `google.protobuf.Timestamp`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hours|integer(int32)|false|none|Hours of day in 24 hour format. Should be from 0 to 23. An API may choose to allow the value "24:00:00" for scenarios like business closing time.|
|minutes|integer(int32)|false|none|Minutes of hour of day. Must be from 0 to 59.|
|nanos|integer(int32)|false|none|Fractions of seconds in nanoseconds. Must be from 0 to 999,999,999.|
|seconds|integer(int32)|false|none|Seconds of minutes of the time. Must normally be from 0 to 59. An API may allow the value 60 if it allows leap-seconds.|

A Treemap chart.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|colorData|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data that determines the background color of each treemap data cell. This field is optional. If not specified, size_data is used to determine background colors. If specified, the data is expected to be numeric. color_scale will determine how the values in this data map to data cell background colors.|
|colorScale|[TreemapChartColorScale](#schematreemapchartcolorscale)|false|none|The color scale for data cells in the treemap chart. Data cells are assigned colors based on their color values. These color values come from color_data, or from size_data if color_data is not specified. Cells with color values less than or equal to min_value will have minValueColor as their background color. Cells with color values greater than or equal to max_value will have maxValueColor as their background color. Cells with color values between min_value and max_value will have background colors on a gradient between minValueColor and maxValueColor, the midpoint of the gradient being midValueColor. Cells with missing or non-numeric color values will have noDataColor as their background color.|
|headerColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The background color for header cells. Deprecated: Use header_color_style.|
|headerColorStyle|[ColorStyle](#schemacolorstyle)|false|none|The background color for header cells. If header_color is also set, this field takes precedence.|
|hideTooltips|boolean|false|none|True to hide tooltips.|
|hintedLevels|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of additional data levels beyond the labeled levels to be shown on the treemap chart. These levels are not interactive and are shown without their labels. Defaults to 0 if not specified.|
|labels|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data that contains the treemap cell labels.|
|levels|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of data levels to show on the treemap chart. These levels are interactive and are shown with their labels. Defaults to 2 if not specified.|
|maxValue|number(double)|false|none|The maximum possible data value. Cells with values greater than this will have the same color as cells with this value. If not specified, defaults to the actual maximum value from color_data, or the maximum value from size_data if color_data is not specified.|
|minValue|number(double)|false|none|The minimum possible data value. Cells with values less than this will have the same color as cells with this value. If not specified, defaults to the actual minimum value from color_data, or the minimum value from size_data if color_data is not specified.|
|parentLabels|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data the contains the treemap cells' parent labels.|
|sizeData|[ChartData](#schemachartdata)|false|none|The data that determines the size of each treemap data cell. This data is expected to be numeric. The cells corresponding to non-numeric or missing data will not be rendered. If color_data is not specified, this data is used to determine data cell background colors as well.|
|textFormat|[TextFormat](#schematextformat)|false|none|The text format for all labels on the chart. The link field is not supported.|

<h2 id="tocS_TrimWhitespaceRequest">TrimWhitespaceRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematrimwhitespacerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_TrimWhitespaceRequest"></a>
<a id="tocStrimwhitespacerequest"></a>
<a id="tocstrimwhitespacerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "range": {
    "endColumnIndex": 0,
    "endRowIndex": 0,
    "sheetId": 0,
    "startColumnIndex": 0,
    "startRowIndex": 0
  }
}
```

Trims the whitespace (such as spaces, tabs, or new lines) in every cell in the specified range. This request removes all whitespace from the start and end of each cell's text, and reduces any subsequence of remaining whitespace characters to a single space. If the resulting trimmed text starts with a '+' or '=' character, the text remains as a string value and isn't interpreted as a formula.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range whose cells to trim.|

Updates properties of the supplied banded range.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bandedRange|[BandedRange](#schemabandedrange)|false|none|The banded range to update with the new properties.|
|fields|string(google-fieldmask)|false|none|The fields that should be updated. At least one field must be specified. The root `bandedRange` is implied and should not be specified. A single `"*"` can be used as short-hand for listing every field.|

Updates the borders of a range. If a field is not set in the request, that means the border remains as-is. For example, with two subsequent UpdateBordersRequest: 1. range: A1:A5 `{ top: RED, bottom: WHITE }` 2. range: A1:A5 `{ left: BLUE }` That would result in A1:A5 having a borders of `{ top: RED, bottom: WHITE, left: BLUE }`. If you want to clear a border, explicitly set the style to NONE.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bottom|[Border](#schemaborder)|false|none|The border to put at the bottom of the range.|
|innerHorizontal|[Border](#schemaborder)|false|none|The horizontal border to put within the range.|
|innerVertical|[Border](#schemaborder)|false|none|The vertical border to put within the range.|
|left|[Border](#schemaborder)|false|none|The border to put at the left of the range.|
|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range whose borders should be updated.|
|right|[Border](#schemaborder)|false|none|The border to put at the right of the range.|
|top|[Border](#schemaborder)|false|none|The border to put at the top of the range.|


Updates all cells in a range with new data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|string(google-fieldmask)|false|none|The fields of CellData that should be updated. At least one field must be specified. The root is the CellData; 'row.values.' should not be specified. A single `"*"` can be used as short-hand for listing every field.|
|range|[GridRange](#schemagridrange)|false|none|The range to write data to. If the data in rows does not cover the entire requested range, the fields matching those set in fields will be cleared.|
|rows|[[RowData](#schemarowdata)]|false|none|The data to write.|
|start|[GridCoordinate](#schemagridcoordinate)|false|none|The coordinate to start writing data at. Any number of rows and columns (including a different number of columns per row) may be written.|


Updates a chart's specifications. (This does not move or resize a chart. To move or resize a chart, use UpdateEmbeddedObjectPositionRequest.)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chartId|integer(int32)|false|none|The ID of the chart to update.|
|spec|[ChartSpec](#schemachartspec)|false|none|The specification to apply to the chart.|

|sheetId|integer(int32)|false|none|The sheet of the rule to move. Required if new_index is set, unused otherwise.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|newIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The index of the new rule.|

|oldRule|[ConditionalFormatRule](#schemaconditionalformatrule)|false|none|The old (deleted) rule. Not set if a rule was moved (because it is the same as new_rule).|

|fields|string(google-fieldmask)|false|none|The fields that should be updated. At least one field must be specified. The root `dataSource` is implied and should not be specified. A single `"*"` can be used as short-hand for listing every field.|

A request to update properties of developer metadata. Updates the properties of the developer metadata selected by the filters to the values provided in the DeveloperMetadata resource. Callers must specify the properties they wish to update in the fields parameter, as well as specify at least one DataFilter matching the metadata they wish to update.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dataFilters|[[DataFilter](#schemadatafilter)]|false|none|The filters matching the developer metadata entries to update.|
|developerMetadata|[DeveloperMetadata](#schemadevelopermetadata)|false|none|The value that all metadata matched by the data filters will be updated to.|
|fields|string(google-fieldmask)|false|none|The fields that should be updated. At least one field must be specified. The root `developerMetadata` is implied and should not be specified. A single `"*"` can be used as short-hand for listing every field.|

Update an embedded object's position (such as a moving or resizing a chart or image).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|string(google-fieldmask)|false|none|The fields of OverlayPosition that should be updated when setting a new position. Used only if newPosition.overlayPosition is set, in which case at least one field must be specified. The root `newPosition.overlayPosition` is implied and should not be specified. A single `"*"` can be used as short-hand for listing every field.|
|newPosition|[EmbeddedObjectPosition](#schemaembeddedobjectposition)|false|none|An explicit position to move the embedded object to. If newPosition.sheetId is set, a new sheet with that ID will be created. If newPosition.newSheet is set to true, a new sheet will be created with an ID that will be chosen for you.|
|objectId|integer(int32)|false|none|The ID of the object to moved.|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|majorDimension|string|false|none|The major dimension of the values. For output, if the spreadsheet data is: `A1=1,B1=2,A2=3,B2=4`, then requesting `range=A1:B2,majorDimension=ROWS` will return `[[1,2],[3,4]]`, whereas requesting `range=A1:B2,majorDimension=COLUMNS` will return `[[1,3],[2,4]]`. For input, with `range=A1:B2,majorDimension=ROWS` then `[[1,2],[3,4]]` will set `A1=1,B1=2,A2=3,B2=4`. With `range=A1:B2,majorDimension=COLUMNS` then `[[1,2],[3,4]]` will set `A1=1,B1=3,A2=2,B2=4`. When writing, if this field is not set, it defaults to ROWS.|
|range|string|false|none|The range the values cover, in [A1 notation](/sheets/api/guides/concepts#cell). For output, this range indicates the entire requested range, even though the values will exclude trailing rows and columns. When appending values, this field represents the range to search for a table, after which values will be appended.|
|values|[[object]]|false|none|The data that was read or to be written. This is an array of arrays, the outer array representing all the data and each inner array representing a major dimension. Each item in the inner array corresponds with one cell. For output, empty trailing rows and columns will not be included. For input, supported value types are: bool, string, and double. Null values will be skipped. To set a cell to an empty value, set the string value to an empty string.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|majorDimension|DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED|
|majorDimension|ROWS|
|majorDimension|COLUMNS|

<h2 id="tocS_WaterfallChartCustomSubtotal">WaterfallChartCustomSubtotal</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawaterfallchartcustomsubtotal"></a>
<a id="schema_WaterfallChartCustomSubtotal"></a>
<a id="tocSwaterfallchartcustomsubtotal"></a>
<a id="tocswaterfallchartcustomsubtotal"></a>

```json
{
  "dataIsSubtotal": true,
  "label": "string",
  "subtotalIndex": 0
}
```

A custom subtotal column for a waterfall chart series.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dataIsSubtotal|boolean|false|none|True if the data point at subtotal_index is the subtotal. If false, the subtotal will be computed and appear after the data point.|
|label|string|false|none|A label for the subtotal column.|
|subtotalIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The zero-based index of a data point within the series. If data_is_subtotal is true, the data point at this index is the subtotal. Otherwise, the subtotal appears after the data point with this index. A series can have multiple subtotals at arbitrary indices, but subtotals do not affect the indices of the data points. For example, if a series has three data points, their indices will always be 0, 1, and 2, regardless of how many subtotals exist on the series or what data points they are associated with.|

|negativeColumnsStyle|[WaterfallChartColumnStyle](#schemawaterfallchartcolumnstyle)|false|none|Styles for all columns in this series with negative values.|
|positiveColumnsStyle|[WaterfallChartColumnStyle](#schemawaterfallchartcolumnstyle)|false|none|Styles for all columns in this series with positive values.|
|subtotalColumnsStyle|[WaterfallChartColumnStyle](#schemawaterfallchartcolumnstyle)|false|none|Styles for all subtotal columns in this series.|

A waterfall chart.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connectorLineStyle|[LineStyle](#schemalinestyle)|false|none|The line style for the connector lines.|
|domain|[WaterfallChartDomain](#schemawaterfallchartdomain)|false|none|The domain data (horizontal axis) for the waterfall chart.|
|firstValueIsTotal|boolean|false|none|True to interpret the first value as a total.|
|hideConnectorLines|boolean|false|none|True to hide connector lines between columns.|
|series|[[WaterfallChartSeries](#schemawaterfallchartseries)]|false|none|The data this waterfall chart is visualizing.|
|stackedType|string|false|none|The stacked type.|
|totalDataLabel|[DataLabel](#schemadatalabel)|false|none|Controls whether to display additional data labels on stacked charts which sum the total value of all stacked values at each value along the domain axis. stacked_type must be STACKED and neither CUSTOM nor placement can be set on the total_data_label.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|stackedType|WATERFALL_STACKED_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|stackedType|STACKED|
|stackedType|SEQUENTIAL|
